findings.topic: K-skill (NomaDamas/k-skill): identity, scale, licence
findings.finding: K-skill is an open-source Korean-life skill bundle from the NomaDamas GitHub organization (repo description: 한국인을 위한 스킬 모음집 - 에이전트를 한국인으로). GitHub metadata read on 2026-09-28: created 2026-03-24, last push 2026-09-21, 7,704 stars, 936 forks, 55 open issues, JavaScript, MIT. The README says 총 125개 스킬 in about 20 category tables (transport/KTX/buses, real estate, law and public services, tax/business, government support, jobs, finance and statistics, health, shopping, food, sports, culture, education, news, Korean writing, weather, daily life, developer tools such as HWP, fortune/naming, plus a setup skill). The count differs by document and date (marketplace.json says 90+, a llms.txt snippet says 118, runtime-action-audit about 127, an awesome-list still says 15), so it is growing fast. Licence: MIT at root; packages/k-skill-proxy and infra/k-skill-proxy-dashboard are AGPL-3.0-only. Claimed hosts: Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw/ClawHub, plus a Manus import guide.
findings.relevance: Use as a structural reference only, as the owner asked not to clone. Do not copy text or code, and keep AGPL proxy code out of an MIT repository. Star and skill counts are point-in-time.

findings.topic: K-skill repository structure and per-skill file layout
findings.finding: Root has .claude-plugin/{marketplace.json,plugin.json}, docs/ (features/<skill>.md with 100+ pages, legal/, sources.md, security-and-secrets.md, setup.md, install.md, adding-a-skill.md, runtime-action-audit.md, browser-runtime.md, roadmap.md, releasing.md), packages/, infra/, examples/, .changeset/. Each skill folder holds skill.json (single source of truth: name, description, profiles, raw frontmatter), instruction.md (sections: what it does, when to use, workflow, Done when, Failure modes such as blanks, blocks, login walls), a generated SKILL.md stub that must not be edited, references/ (DISCLAIMER.md and TRADEMARK-LEGAL-STATEMENT.md), scripts/ and tests. Implementation types are instruction-only, npm package, proxy, or Python script. A lint (npm run ci) checks that every dir has SKILL.md, frontmatter starts with ---, name equals the directory name, and stub/source/bundle stay consistent. README skill tables use Korean columns 할 수 있는 일 / 스킬 이름 / 설명 plus a login-requirement note and link to a per-skill feature doc. Maintainers write a legal-review issue per skill (see legal finding).
findings.relevance: Adopt the ideas of a per-source doc, explicit 'Done when' and 'Failure modes' sections in each research reference, and a consistency lint. Do not adopt the runtime CLI part (next finding).

findings.topic: K-skill SKILL.md stubs load their real instructions from an npm CLI at run time
findings.finding: The generated SKILL.md of each skill (checked: naver-blog-research, naver-news-search, kosis-stats, k-skill-setup) carries an HTML comment marking it as a generated CLI stub and tells the agent to run npx -y @nomadamas/k-skill@0 instruct <skill-name> and follow the output as the primary instructions. The CLI detects the runtime and prints only applicable instructions. Anthropic's Skills documentation warns that skills which fetch external content are a particular risk and should be audited.
findings.relevance: Avoid for Remorsearch. It puts network-fetched text in the instruction position, which conflicts with the rule that external content is data and never followed, and adds offline and supply-chain failure modes. Keep instructions static and versioned in the repo. Only the build-time 'single source generates the stub' idea is worth borrowing, if at all. The risk judgement is my inference; the behaviour is verbatim from the repo.

findings.topic: Naming, frontmatter and metadata conventions
findings.finding: Anthropic's spec requires name to be ASCII lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, at most 64 characters, without the reserved words anthropic or claude, so Korean skills use English kebab-case slugs and put Korean into descriptions. K-skill names are service-slug plus function (naver-news-search, kosis-stats, k-dart, kbo-results), a korean- prefix for language and knowledge skills, and frontmatter metadata {category, locale: ko-KR, phase: v1}; in Claude Code plugin skills are namespaced /k-skill:<skill>. opendata-kr names repos <service-slug>-mcp; Koomook/data-go-mcp-servers uses one package per API. K-skill's rule (write descriptions in Korean for Korean services) is not enforced: naver-news-search and kosis-stats have Korean one-line descriptions ending in plain declarative 한다체 (조회한다, 정리한다), while naver-blog-research and k-skill-setup are English.
findings.relevance: Keep the ASCII name remorsearch-ux-qa. For any Korean-focused sub-skill or reference use an ASCII slug with a ko- or korean- prefix. A metadata.locale field is a K-skill habit; whether other hosts tolerate it is unverified. Pick one description language policy and lint it (K-skill shows what drift looks like).

findings.topic: Korean trigger phrases actually used in Korean collections
findings.finding: K-skill keeps utterances in instruction.md 'when to use' (read only after activation) as full natural requests in 해줘체: 오늘 [주제] 관련 뉴스 찾아줘; 최근 [주제] 기사 최신순으로; 네이버 블로그에서 검색해줘; 블로그 글 읽어줘; 1인 가구 비율 통계 찾아줘; KOSIS에서 고령인구 비율 시도별 데이터 가져와; korean-humanizer: 이 글 AI 티 안 나게 다듬어줘 and a detect-only form (AI 흔적만 찾아줘). It also lists what a skill will not do and a 'Not for' list (paywalled full text, bypassing blocks). gptaku insane-research puts English 'This skill should be used when...' plus quoted Korean utterances inside the description itself: 리서치해줘, 딥리서치, 심층 연구, [주제]에 대해 리서치해줘, and mirrors the user's language in prompts and output labels. SoDam-Persona-Codex keeps 43 Korean trigger patterns in one persona-triggers skill, including depth toggles (깊게, 철저히 versus 간단히, which always wins) and evidence toggles (근거, 출처, 사례, 팩트, 출처 검증, 공식 원문).
findings.relevance: Proposal (my synthesis, not observed elsewhere): extend the Korean tail of the description with natural requests such as UX 리서치해줘, 사용자 불만 조사해줘, 후기 모아서 정리해줘, 커뮤니티 반응 봐줘, 대상 사용자 조사해줘, 페르소나 근거 만들어줘, 사용성 테스트해줘, 한 손 조작 점검해줘, and add depth and evidence toggles (간단히/깊게, 근거 붙여서, 출처 검증). Put a Korean 'Not for / 하지 않는 일' list in the research workflow. Whether explicit Korean phrases improve matching on Codex is unverified.

findings.topic: SKILL.md frontmatter safety for Korean text (Claude Code and Codex)
findings.finding: Verified in Anthropic docs: name at most 64 chars; description non-empty, at most 1,024 chars, no XML tags, written in third person with what and when. Claude Code caps combined description plus when_to_use at 1,536 chars in the skill listing (key use first), offers a Claude-Code-specific when_to_use field for trigger phrases, and, if the YAML does not parse, loads the skill with no fields set and no visible error (run with --debug). gptaku_plugins issue #4: 17 of 39 SKILL.md silently lost metadata because an unquoted description contained 'Korean triggers: ' (colon plus space); claude plugin validate still passed; fix is a quoted string or folded block scalar. Codex shows the same class (openai/codex #8609 invalid YAML 'mapping values are not allowed'), a UTF-8 BOM before --- makes a skill unloadable (openai/codex #13918, open), and CJK-Windows code pages (cp949, cp932, cp936) crash Python that reads UTF-8 without an encoding (openai/codex #41028, open). One third-party repo claims non-ASCII or over-long descriptions fail silently in Codex CLI; that is a single unverified source.
findings.relevance: Add a test: frontmatter parses with a real YAML parser, no BOM, description at most 1,024 chars, no angle brackets, single line or quoted or >- block. The current description is 715 chars, parses, and has no colon-space; about 300 chars remain for more Korean triggers. Local finding: scripts/smoke_loop.py lines 54 and 68 call read_text()/write_text() without encoding while handling the Korean string 상품 상세 보기, a portability risk on cp949 Windows; other file I/O is binary or explicit.

findings.topic: Codex metadata file agents/openai.yaml
findings.finding: Search results and GitHub issues indicate Codex reads optional agents/openai.yaml with interface.display_name, interface.short_description, interface.default_prompt and policy.allow_implicit_invocation (default true; false means the skill is only used when named explicitly, for example $skill-name). OpenAI's skill-creator sample names display_name, short_description and default_prompt as the generated fields. The repo's file currently has only English display_name and short_description.
findings.relevance: A Korean short_description and a Korean default_prompt are possible localization points, but the official Codex page was not readable here, so field limits and how Korean renders in the Codex UI are unverified. Test on a real Codex install before shipping.

findings.topic: Bilingual README and repo-presentation patterns
findings.finding: gptaku_plugins: English README.md canonical plus README.ko/zh/ja/es.md, a language-switcher line at the top, and the same skeleton in every language: three-step install, 'start here' flagship plugins each with a 'Try this' prompt, a problem-to-plugin decision table, a trust and credentials table (Claude Code only / Google OAuth / external dependencies), and a catalog by function; Korean voice is friendly 반말/해요 blend. SoDam-Persona-Codex: Korean README.md as source of truth plus README.en.md parity, and a validate.mjs script checking 15 consistency metrics. K-skill: Korean-first, all issues, PRs and reviews in Korean, sections 설치 / 어떤 걸 할 수 있나 / 처음 시작하는 순서 / 문서 / 라이선스 / 컨트리뷰터 / 협력사, a playful communal tone (a Sejong-themed landing page repo too), and a rule that agents must not star the repo without user consent. awesome-korean-agent-skills marks language with 한국어 (skill itself Korean), 영+한 (English content, Korean docs), 다국어(KO), and keeps a host compatibility matrix (CC, GC, CX, CP, OC, CR, WS). MCP wrappers use README.md plus README-ko.md or README-EN.md. K-skill repo titles and forks list Korean service names as search keywords.
findings.relevance: Current README is English with a short 한국어 요약 at the end and no .claude-plugin manifest. Adopt: a README.ko.md with identical headings and a top language switcher, a parity check test, a host-compatibility table with a language marker, and Korean keywords in the GitHub About and topics. Tone suggestion (inference): 합니다체 with one warm line; skip gimmicks that undercut an evidence-first pitch.

findings.topic: Korean report tone and wording conventions
findings.finding: DaleSeo/korean-skills style-guide sets register by document type: business or official 합니다체 used consistently; academic ~이다; technical 합니다 mixed with ~한다; marketing and blog ~해요. It also asks for one term per concept (사용자 versus 유저 versus 이용자), foreign-word notation following 국립국어원 rules, 'YYYY년 MM월 DD일' in business prose versus ISO 8601 in technical records, and lets brand guidelines override. K-skill naver-news-search frames results as '기사 요약에 따르면', quotes only source text, formats times as 'KST YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm', and forbids speculation about individuals. SoDam's evidence persona tags unconfirmed items 미확인 or 제한, records date, version and conflicting sources, says 현재 검색 불가 instead of inventing a citation, and adds domain disclaimers such as 일반 정보 제공용이며 전문가 확인을 권장.
findings.relevance: Current output-template.md is English with a bilingual annex heading (미확정 / Unresolved). Proposal: a Korean report variant in 합니다체, ledger and evidence lines in 개조식 (~함/~임) or 한다체, fixed labels 관찰됨 / 추론 / 미확인 for observed / inferred / unknown, KST dates, a glossary choice for 사용자 or 이용자, and a hedged attribution template such as 작성자는 ~라고 적었습니다 (작성자 진술, 사실 여부 미확인). The facts are verified; the template is a proposal.

findings.topic: Guardrails for a Korean 'AI tone' polishing pass
findings.finding: DaleSeo humanizer targets 40 patterns in six categories (punctuation, spacing, part-of-speech diversity, vocabulary, structure, translationese such as ~에 대해, ~를 통해, ~되어진다, ~할 수 있다) and preserves the source register. K-skill korean-humanizer lists 60+ markers with severity S1 to S3, offers a detect-only mode, and enforces four rules: meaning unchanged, evidence-based edits, genre consistency, no excessive rewriting; it warns when more than 30 percent changes and halts above 50 percent for human review.
findings.relevance: If a Korean polish step is added to report generation, restrict it to prose: never touch verbatim quotes, evidence IDs, status labels, numbers or URLs; cap the change ratio; allow detect-only. Use the translationese list as a lint for the Korean report template rather than a rewriting engine.

findings.topic: Secrets and key handling; the 'missing credential' rule
findings.finding: K-skill's security doc: user-facing variables are namespaced KSKILL_<SERVICE>_<ITEM> (KSKILL_KOSIS_API_KEY, KSKILL_KSTARTUP_API_KEY, KSKILL_RISS_API_KEY, KSKILL_POPBILL_*); resolution order is agent vault capability, injected environment, host vault (1Password, Bitwarden, Keychain), then ~/.config/k-skill/secrets.env (plain dotenv, mode 0600), then a secure prompt; secrets never go into chat, logs, command arguments or git; no example real passwords in docs; scripts/check-setup.sh verifies the setup; a k-skill-setup skill guides key acquisition. Verbatim principle: 인증이 필요한 스킬에서 필요한 값이 없으면 우회하지 않는다, and forbidden is auto-adopting another service or an unofficial workaround because a secret is missing.
findings.relevance: Matches the owner's boundary almost word for word. Adopt: a missing key becomes a recorded gap (for example no_key) and a question to the user, never a silent fall-back to scraping or another site. Namespace new variables REMORSEARCH_<SERVICE>_<ITEM> or document the existing NAVER_* and YOUTUBE_API_KEY names, reuse ~/.config/remorsearch-ux-qa/ (already used by agent-setup), and add a check-setup command.

findings.topic: K-skill proxy-first model (avoid) versus bring-your-own-key
findings.finding: Free and public APIs (Naver news, Kakao Local and Mobility, NEIS school meals, default KOSIS) go through a shared hosted proxy, k-skill-proxy.nomadamas.org (AGPL-3.0-only, 5-minute cache, 60 requests per minute), which injects operator-held keys (NAVER_SEARCH_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, KAKAO_REST_API_KEY sent as Authorization: KakaoAK, KEDU_INFO_KEY, LAW_OC), so users need no keys. Policy: only free APIs use the proxy; paid, per-user or personal-credential APIs must not; direct mode needs the user's own KSKILL_* key. User queries transit the operator. Issues show operating pain (#568 429 spike, #641 403/429/404 analysis).
findings.relevance: Do not adopt: it conflicts with the own-key boundary, sends research queries to a third party, and for the Naver Search API is legally fragile after the 2026 terms change (see Naver finding). Adopt only the direct-with-own-key path plus per-API guardrails: no retry loops on 400 or 429, narrow the query instead, expose cache and requested_at metadata.

findings.topic: Public data portal and statistics wrappers; source registry and 공공누리 attribution
findings.finding: On data.go.kr each API needs its own 활용신청 and the user's own service key from the account page. K-skill's setup doc names DATA_GO_KR_API_KEY, KEDU_INFO_KEY, DATA4LIBRARY_AUTH_KEY, a free KOSIS key from kosis.kr/openapi, the 법제처 LAW_OC from open.law.go.kr, and KIPRIS_PLUS_API_KEY. Koomook/data-go-mcp-servers uses API_KEY with one package per API (Apache-2.0). opendata-kr repos are <service>-mcp and state they are independent of and unaffiliated with data.go.kr. JunsikChoi/korea-cli embeds a 12,119-API catalog for offline Korean-language search and calls APIs only with the user's own key. K-skill docs/sources.md records per service: official surface URL, route (direct, proxy or browser fallback), auth (key, session wall, none), licence or attribution (for example 공공누리 제1유형 출처표시), limits, and a dated observation; it separates a documented Open API from an observed web surface, and uses a user-downloaded CSV as fallback when a live API fails.
findings.relevance: Create a Korean source registry with the same columns plus observed_at and verified_at, and store 공공누리 type as attribution metadata for any public-data statistic. Keep the API key acquisition steps (활용신청 per API, approval delay) in a setup note. All portal hosts were blocked here, so the key-acquisition steps are unverified against official pages.

findings.topic: KOSIS provenance card and staged retrieval
findings.finding: K-skill kosis-stats wraps KOSIS Open API search, metadata and data calls. Key: KSKILL_KOSIS_API_KEY (free from kosis.kr/openapi) for direct mode. Its instruction requires every answer to carry source, orgId, tblId, reference period (기준 시점), unit (UNIT_NM) and the endpoint URL, and prescribes staged retrieval: find the table, read metadata to confirm classification, unit and period, pull a small slice, then widen. It documents error codes with recovery paths and a 'Done when' list (table ID fixed, metadata read at least once, staged pull, source stated, remedy offered when limits are hit). The description names 국가데이터처 as KOSIS's operator (K-skill's wording; not independently verified).
findings.relevance: For the audience pipeline, make every official statistic a provenance card: 기관, 통계표명, tblId, 기준시점, 단위, URL, 조회일. Keep it in the existing 'statistical' source family, where it bounds a segment and never equals a product's user base. Example trigger from K-skill: 1인 가구 비율 통계 찾아줘. Quota figures in the K-skill doc were not verified.

findings.topic: How K-skill and MCP wrappers handle Naver
findings.finding: Three approaches. (a) naver-news-search: Naver Search Open API via the proxy with operator keys; strips HTML, formats KST times, does not retry on 400 or 429, notes Naver's combined 25,000 calls per day, keeps no persistent query log and never fetches full articles. (b) naver-blog-research: python-stdlib reading of search.naver.com blog result pages and blog post pages (mobile URLs), no key, at most 30 results per query and 10 images per session, framed as small-scale non-commercial; it reads no comments and does not label or grade sponsored posts; issue #465 records hidden accessibility labels appended to titles and snippets. (c) isnow890/naver-search-mcp (MIT): own keys via NAVER_CLIENT_ID and NAVER_CLIENT_SECRET, or the newer NCP_APIGW_API_KEY_ID and NCP_APIGW_API_KEY; tools for webkr, news, blog, cafearticle, image, kin, encyc, local plus DataLab; shopping, book and academic tools were removed in v1.0.49 after those APIs ended.
findings.relevance: Do not adopt (b): reading search-result pages violates the project's rule never to scrape search-result pages. Reusable: the volume caps, KST time format, no full-text mirroring, snippet cleaning of hidden labels. The project's Korean sponsorship markers already go beyond (b). Note (c)'s key names differ from the NAVER_* names in the project's planned discover command.

findings.topic: Naver policy changes, Aug to Sep 2026 (affects Naver API and Cafe use)
findings.finding: Reported by several Korean outlets and search summaries; the primary Naver text could not be read here. (1) Search API special terms revised, effective 2026-09-07 (one English report says updated 2026-09-08): feeding search API data into AI, or using it to train, improve, evaluate or expose in AI services, is banned; copying or storing it and giving or selling it to third parties is banned in principle; results are to be shown as provided. (2) Search API moves from Naver Developers to NAVER API HUB on NAVER Cloud Platform: new applications at Developers closed 2026-07-31, old keys work until 2027-06-30, shopping, book and academic search ended 2026-07-31 with no replacement, blog, cafearticle, news, webkr, image, kin, local plus DataLab trends move to API HUB with new host, headers and keys, and usage-based billing is reported. (3) A Naver Cafe notice (reported 2026-08-31) prohibits bulk collection of posts and comments without member and cafe consent, including by crawlers, bots or scripts, via non-official routes, or by getting around blocks, and states legal action; Naver says this notice is not specifically about AI training and that AI crawling of user-generated content has been blocked by default since last year.
findings.relevance: High impact. references/research/public-page-access.md section 12 and workflow.md step 2 plan ux_research.py discover (planned) to call the Naver Search Open API (blog, cafe articles, 지식iN, news) with NAVER_CLIENT_ID and NAVER_CLIENT_SECRET as lead sources. Those are legacy key names, and if the reported clause holds, an agent ingesting the results is the prohibited use. Proposal: add a stop class such as terms_restricted (platform terms bar AI ingestion), mark the Naver Search API 'user-operated only, agent does not ingest results' until the owner reads the primary terms, treat Naver Cafe as user-supplied evidence (user opens and quotes a few public posts, no bulk, default deny_hosts), and re-check the Naver Cafe and blog rows in section 15. K-skill's naver-news-search legal-review issue closed 2026-08-17, before the 2026-09-07 effective date, and I found no maintainer response; that is an inference from dates.

findings.topic: Kakao wrappers and the user-supplied export lane
findings.finding: K-skill kakao-map wraps Kakao Local and Kakao Mobility through the proxy with an operator-held KAKAO_REST_API_KEY (Authorization: KakaoAK), about 1,000 Mobility requests per day, 5-minute cache, vehicle routing only, no booking or payment. kakaotalk-mac reads and searches the user's own local KakaoTalk archive through the katok CLI on Apple Silicon macOS with user-granted Full Disk Access, and explicitly excludes sending, deleting, UI automation, direct database reading, auth-cache handling and decryption material. lumin-on/claude-skills kakao-chat-analysis turns a user-exported KakaoTalk .txt into an HTML plus PDF discussion report; no anonymization step is documented and the repo ships only synthetic samples. Kakao Developers' Daum Search API covers web, video, image, blog, book and cafe search with a REST API key and daily and monthly quotas; its AI-use terms were not verified.
findings.relevance: KakaoTalk open chat stays out of scope (private, as in the current channel notes). A user-supplied export lane (interview notes, team chats, store-console CSVs) is legitimate only with consent and a mandatory anonymization step (names, phone numbers) before analysis; never read app databases. Daum Cafe or blog search via the official API is an option only after checking Kakao's terms.

findings.topic: Per-source legal disclaimers, legal-review records and Korean legal citations
findings.finding: Each K-skill skill ships references/DISCLAIMER.md and TRADEMARK-LEGAL-STATEMENT.md; docs/legal/ holds trademark-use-review.md and read-only-skill-risk-resolution.md; each skill has a legal-review issue (#492 naver-shopping-search, #494 naver-blog-research, #500 naver-ad-performance, #543 naver-news-search, closed 2026-08-17). Wording is formal Korean: not an official feature, no affiliation, sponsorship or approval, brand names used descriptively only. The naver-news-search disclaimer cites Supreme Court 2005도1637 (2005-06-10, descriptive use versus source indicator), Supreme Court 2021도1533 (2022-05-12), Trademark Act arts. 2, 89, 90, 108, Network Act art. 48, Copyright Act art. 93 and Penal Code art. 314(2). The read-only legal review lists seven risks (trademark, database and copyright rights, unauthorized access, terms breach, personal information, attribution confusion, scope creep) with mitigations: prefer official web or API surfaces, no authentication bypass, respect quotas, minimal retention, drop personal data such as names and phone numbers, no logos, and it calls itself an internal record and not a legal opinion. README limits public-information lookup to personal, non-organizational use, no mass or systematic crawling, no access-control evasion. Case 2021도1533 was confirmed via the Supreme Court site summary: acquittal affirmed for a company that crawled a competitor's mobile-app API server, on network-intrusion, database-right and computer-obstruction charges (a criminal case on its own facts).
findings.relevance: Adopt a per-source 'unofficial, no affiliation' note and a 'legal note (unverified, not legal advice)' field in the Korean source registry. Do not import K-skill's personal-use posture as is, since UX research is organizational; state the skill's own posture (user-directed, small-scale, no archiving or redistribution, user checks terms). Never present 2021도1533 as permission to read. The statute citations are K-skill's and were not verified on law.go.kr.

findings.topic: Action-safety taxonomy and typed stop codes
findings.finding: K-skill's runtime-action-audit sorts capabilities into eight modes (Lookup, Local, Commerce, Booking, Submission, Legal, Recruiting, Operations); irreversible actions need a 'clarify' approval of the exact payload; CAPTCHA and identity verification are treated as non-bypassable boundaries. docs/browser-runtime.md 'Stop rules' defines seven typed codes: AUTH_REQUIRED, CAPTCHA_DETECTED, PAYMENT_REQUIRED, ELECTRONIC_SIGNATURE, IRREVERSIBLE_BOUNDARY, BLOCKED, UNAVAILABLE, each with a handler, and the agent names the stop reason to the user. The setup doc adds that public-data queries prefer direct HTTP before browser automation. I did not read or evaluate the runtime-specific browser sections of that doc (outside our no-evasion boundary).
findings.relevance: The project already has richer classes in public-page-access.md section 5 (opted_out, gone, auth_gate, paywall, human_check, rate_limit, geo_block, legal_block, budget, host_stopped) with Korean markers (회원만, 본인인증, 성인인증, 보안문자). Mapping: AUTH_REQUIRED to auth_gate, CAPTCHA_DETECTED to human_check, BLOCKED to bot_filter or host_stopped; the payment, signature and irreversible codes do not apply to a read-only mode. Gaps to consider: terms_restricted (platform terms bar AI ingestion), no_key or quota (missing credential), and whether markers.json covers Korean login prompts such as 휴대폰 인증, 공동인증서, 간편인증 (not checked).

findings.topic: Other Korean-focused skill and plugin collections (landscape)
findings.finding: fivetaku/gptaku_plugins: MIT, about 1.2k stars, 18 plugins as git submodules (insane-search, insane-research, git-teacher, vibe-sunsang and others), marketplace layout, per-plugin DISCLAIMER.md and CHANGELOG.md, gptaku_doctor.py seven-axis validation, release rule that the tag equals the plugin.json version. DaleSeo/korean-skills: MIT, 216 stars, three Korean-writing skills (humanizer, grammar-checker, style-guide) with Korean SKILL.md bodies. sodam-ai/SoDam-Persona-Codex: Apache-2.0, a Codex plugin (.codex-plugin/plugin.json, hooks, 31 skills, 43 Korean triggers, validate.mjs). x77xdavid-prog/checkup-skills: MIT, small marketplace (ko-writer, naver-seo-check, korea-public-data and others), no adoption yet. bear2u/my-skills: MIT, about 933 stars, Korean descriptions. lumin-on/claude-skills: kakao-chat-analysis. MCP wrappers: isnow890/naver-search-mcp (MIT), chrisryugj/korean-law-mcp (MIT), Koomook/data-go-mcp-servers (Apache-2.0), opendata-kr (MIT), JunsikChoi/korea-cli (MIT). Indexes: J-nowcow/awesome-korean-agent-skills (451+ skills, monthly link checks) and yunsell/ai-agent-skills-korean.
findings.relevance: Reference set for structure only; all star and fork counts are point-in-time on 2026-09-28. gptaku's positioning of insane-search around getting past blocks sits outside our boundary, so only its structure is relevant.

findings.topic: Ecosystem gap and Korean sponsorship-disclosure context
findings.finding: Searches for Korean community-opinion analysis (DC Inside, Clien, Ppomppu, TheQoo), Korean app-review analysis and Korean UX-research skills found no Korean-specific skill. App-review skills found are global (AyaTarek91/app-reviews-skill, PuHuaKuang/google-play-reviews-skills); UX-research skills are English (uh-joan/ux-research-skills); the awesome-korean list has no research or UX category; gptaku insane-research grades sources A to E with no Korean source taxonomy; K-skill's naver-blog-research does no ad labelling. Regulatory background for Korean review culture: the KFTC 추천·보증 등에 관한 표시·광고 심사지침 requires disclosing economic interests in recommendations and reviews; search summaries report a 2026-04-08 amendment notice on labelling AI-generated virtual persons (for blogs and cafes, in the title or the opening lines) and an earlier 2024 change to disclosure placement on social media.
findings.relevance: Differentiators for Remorsearch are already partly built: Korean sponsorship markers (체험단, 협찬, 원고료, 제공받아, 쿠팡 파트너스 and more) in source-grading.md and uxresearch/data/markers.json with a grade-D cap. Possible additions: cite the KFTC guideline as the basis for those markers (verify the text on law.go.kr; blocked here), add a Korean source taxonomy, Korean evidence labels, and the user-supplied evidence lane. A negative search result is not proof that no such skill exists.

findings.topic: Korean legal-citation verification pattern
findings.finding: chrisryugj/korean-law-mcp (MIT) wraps the 법제처 Open API with the user's own LAW_OC key (free from open.law.go.kr) and includes a verify_citations tool that checks AI-produced statute and case citations against the official database, flagging non-existent articles and article-number versus title mismatches (verified, not found, mismatch). Other law MCPs exist (seo-jinseok, finalchild, milkis-zero). K-skill has korean-law-search (operator-side LAW_OC) and korean-privacy-terms, a wrapper of kimlawtech/korean-privacy-terms (Apache-2.0) that labels output 'reference draft, not legal advice, get attorney review' and says it reflects a personal-information-law amendment effective 2026-09-11 (unverified by me).
findings.relevance: For any law or regulation claim in a report (개인정보 보호법, 공정위 지침, platform terms), add a citation check: the article exists on law.go.kr and its title matches, otherwise label 미확인. Where law.go.kr is unreachable, record 'not verified' rather than assert.

findings.topic: Distribution and packaging conventions
findings.finding: K-skill installs through the Claude Code marketplace (/plugin marketplace add NomaDamas/k-skill, /plugin install k-skill@k-skill, invoked as /k-skill:<skill>), through npx --yes skills add NomaDamas/k-skill --all -g (or --skill <name>; pnpm dlx and bunx equivalents), an npm CLI @nomadamas/k-skill (instruct, version, update), .skill bundles for drag-and-drop upload, and a Manus guide. marketplace.json holds name, owner and plugins [{name, source './', description}]. Requirements are stated in Korean install docs (Node 18+, Python 3.11 with uv only where needed). Releases use Changesets. SoDam shows a Codex layout (.codex-plugin/plugin.json plus .agents/plugins/marketplace.json), single source.
findings.relevance: The repo has no .claude-plugin/ manifest and installs by copying the folder. Adopt: a marketplace manifest, a per-host install table in Korean and English, and keep the copy path. Do not add a run-time instruct CLI. The Codex plugin layout is from one source and unverified.

findings.topic: Validation tooling in Korean collections
findings.finding: K-skill npm run ci checks SKILL.md presence, frontmatter, name equals directory and stub/source/bundle consistency, and the pre-PR checklist covers secret naming and typed stop rules for browser-dependent skills. SoDam validate.mjs checks 15 metrics (perspective count, trigger IDs, skill folders, manifest versions, disclaimer enforcement). gptaku_doctor.py validates seven axes (enablement, cache consistency, version alignment, commit SHA, release tags).
findings.relevance: Add tests for: frontmatter lint (see the safety finding), README.md versus README.ko.md heading parity, Korean marker list sanity, and Korean source-registry rows having official URL, route, auth, licence and observed_at.

findings.topic: Aside and automation-browser fallbacks (tangential)
findings.finding: K-skill docs/sources.md names 'Aside Browser' as an automated fallback for a public government page when direct HTTP times out, explicitly not the user's own logged-in session. Third-party guides describe Aside as an agentic Chromium browser (YC Fall 2025) that can be attached to MCP clients such as Claude Code; needsbuilder/bside publishes a benchmark on five Korean-web errands claiming Aside's own agent was fastest but that Aside driven as a CLI by a coding agent lost to Playwright (unverified claim).
findings.relevance: Supports the existing tool order (the user's real browser first). Label any such fallback in the access record as 'automation browser, not user session'. I did not verify the benchmark.

findings.topic: Project cross-check: what already exists locally (avoid duplicate work)
findings.finding: Read-only checks of /home/user/ux-research-qa-skills: SKILL.md description is 715 chars, parses as YAML, has no colon-space, and already ends with Korean keywords (UX 리서치, 대상 사용자 리서치, UX QA, 사용성 테스트, 페르소나 QA); no BOM in md, py, json or yaml files; README is English with a 한국어 요약 section; no .claude-plugin/; public-page-access.md already has typed stop classes with Korean markers, Korean channel notes (Naver blog, Cafe, 지식iN, Tistory, DCInside, Ppomppu, Ruliweb, FMKorea, Clien, theqoo, App Store, Google Play) and robots and volume rules (8 s plus 0 to 4 s jitter per host); workflow.md has Korean query templates ([service] 불편, 후기, 갈아탄 이유) and a Korean-first language policy for Korean products; source-grading.md and markers.json already carry Korean sponsorship markers; output-template.md is English with the annex heading 미확정 / Unresolved; docs/human-factors/korean-population-context.md uses evidence tags [P] [D] [S] [2] [X] [R] and records that kosis.kr, law.go.kr and gallup.co.kr were blocked in that session.
findings.relevance: Priorities that remain open after this cross-check: Korean report register and labels, README.ko.md plus manifest, a Korean source registry with terms and licence fields, terms_restricted and no_key stop or gap classes, the Naver discover plan (section 12), Codex or Claude frontmatter lint, and an encoding fix in smoke_loop.py.

findings.topic: Adopt / adapt / avoid summary
findings.finding: ADOPT (structure, no text copied): missing-credential rule (stop and ask, never switch to an unofficial route); namespaced secret names with a 0600 dotenv or vault order and never in chat, logs or examples; provenance card for official statistics; a per-source registry with official surface, route, auth, licence and observed date, separating documented APIs from observed web surfaces; per-source unofficial and trademark note plus a legal-note field marked unverified; 'Done when' and 'Failure modes' plus a Korean 'not for' list in each reference; full natural Korean utterances and depth or evidence toggles as triggers; a bilingual README skeleton with a parity test; frontmatter, BOM and encoding lint; a marketplace manifest. ADAPT: typed stop codes into the existing stop classes (add terms_restricted and no_key); K-skill volume caps into run budgets; Korean register by document type into a Korean report variant; AI-tone patterns as lint on prose only. AVOID: shared operator proxy with hidden keys; run-time instruction loading through npx instruct; reading search-result pages (naver-blog-research approach); the personal-use-only legal posture as a claim of legality; any bypass-oriented components or runtime-specific browser material (not investigated); ingesting Naver Search API results into the agent until the primary terms are read.
findings.relevance: Consolidates the findings above for the planning step; each item traces to a numbered finding. Recommendations are my synthesis; the factual bases carry the confidence given in their own findings.

gaps: Blocked or unreadable hosts: k-skill.nomadamas.org (llms.txt, homepage) and the k-skill-proxy privacy page, developers.naver.com and all Naver hosts (including robots.txt for blog, cafe and search), ncloud.com, developers.kakao.com, developers.openai.com, agentskills.io, and the Korean news sites (newsis, tokenpost, newsway, dataeconomy, digitaltoday). Their content comes from search-result summaries or GitHub mirrors, not the pages themselves.

Naver Search API terms: the primary clause text was not read. Unresolved: exact wording and scope (does 'AI input' cover a user's own local agent reading results), whether Developers Center and API HUB terms differ, and the effective date (2026-09-07 in Korean reports versus 2026-09-08 in one English report). The owner or a legal reviewer must read the primary NAVER Cloud and Naver terms and Cafe notice before deciding.
Naver blog, cafe and search robots.txt could not be fetched, so I cannot say whether the project's R2 mobile-twin reads of Naver Cafe or blog pages pass the project's own opted_out rule.
Kakao and Daum Search API terms (AI use, quotas) not verified; only a search summary and a quota thread were seen.

Codex behaviour with Korean (non-ASCII) descriptions is unverified: the openai/codex issues found concern colon-space, BOM and cp949 read errors; only one third-party issue claims silent failure for non-ASCII or long descriptions. Codex agents/openai.yaml field limits and Korean rendering are unverified (docs blocked).

WebFetch answers come from a small summarising model. I re-requested verbatim quotes only for the load-bearing K-skill claims (personal-use sentence, licence split, 125 count, missing-credential rule, seven stop codes, naver-blog-research frontmatter); other details (README section order, category tables, sample utterances, kosis-stats behaviour, KFTC details) are medium confidence. Numbers such as KOSIS quotas were deliberately left out as unverified.

K-skill skill counts are inconsistent across documents (90+, 118, 125, about 127) and star counts are point-in-time; the docs/features listing was truncated at 100 entries; per-skill references were checked only for naver-news-search; the k-skill-proxy source was not read.
K-skill's response, if any, to Naver's September 2026 terms change was not found in the issues I could read; community reception of K-skill (GeekNews and similar) was not found.

K-skill also contains runtime-specific browser material and named runtimes (Dolshoi, CloakBrowser) that I deliberately did not read or evaluate, because they fall outside the no-evasion boundary; nothing from them is recommended.
The negative finding that no Korean community-analysis, app-review or UX-research skill exists rests on a handful of searches and is not proof of absence.

Korean statutes and cases cited by K-skill (Copyright Act arts. 91 and 93, Network Act art. 48, Personal Information Protection Act art. 3 and the claimed 2026-09-11 amendment, Trademark Act articles, Supreme Court 2005도1637) were not verified on law.go.kr; only 2021도1533 was identified through the Supreme Court site summary and case-note listing, and the KFTC guideline details come from search summaries.

Not checked: whether uxresearch/data/markers.json already covers Korean login prompts such as 휴대폰 인증, 공동인증서 and 간편인증; whether other hosts tolerate a metadata.locale frontmatter field; Korean stop-marker and channel-note accuracy against live sites.

findings.topic: Method and evidence quality (read first)
findings.finding: Every platform fact below was seen only as search-engine result summaries, plus a few GitHub files I could actually open (Naver's official OpenAPI swagger, K-skill docs, GitHub issues and PRs). Nearly every other host (datareportal, wiseapp, reuters, developers.naver.com, developers.kakao.com, developers.google.com, law.go.kr, ftc.go.kr, news sites, and the community sites) was refused by the network egress proxy, and the 200-call web-search budget ran out before every platform was covered. Under the skill's own source-grading rules these are leads (snippet or summarising fetch, at most D). 'high' below means several independent results agree or an official primary URL surfaced and its content was reflected consistently; it does not mean a live check was done. No community site was fetched.
findings.relevance: Re-verify anything you plan to encode as a route, marker or claim with `ux_research.py robots` plus a human read of the primary page; keep the 'unverified' label until then.

findings.topic: Cross-platform: app reach in Korea (Wiseapp 2025)
findings.finding: Wiseapp-Retail (a commercial app-usage panel, Android+iOS, reported sample 80,000+ smartphone users or about 0.2%, then extrapolated) gives average monthly users for Jan-Nov 2025: KakaoTalk 48.23M, YouTube 46.78M, Google 45.10M, Naver 44.09M, Chrome 42.03M, Coupang 33.88M, Naver Map 30.44M, Instagram 27.03M, Toss 24.94M, Baemin 22.26M; YouTube took the most total time (about 114 billion minutes per month). For Feb 2025 SNS/community apps: Instagram 26.44M, Band 17.38M, Naver Cafe 9.52M, Facebook 7.67M, X 7.51M, TikTok 7.43M, Threads 5.93M (+133% year on year). Navigation apps Jan-Oct 2025 (estimated 51.22M smartphone users): Naver Map is the top app for 20s, T map for 30+.
findings.relevance: Good for ordering channels by reach and as `estimate`-family (C) context. It counts app users, not people who post, and cannot set a segment share. Naver Cafe/Blog, Danggeun, Coupang and Naver Map all sit in the top tier, so they belong in the route table even where access is hard.

findings.topic: Cross-platform: survey reach by age, and why numbers disagree
findings.finding: KPF (Korea Press Foundation) 2024 social media user survey: KakaoTalk 98.9%, YouTube 84.9%, Instagram 38.6%, Band 28.6%, Naver Blog 21.7%; average 4.25 platforms per person; Instagram 80.9% of 20s and 70.7% of 30s; Band 40.6% of 50s and 31.1% of 60s. Gallup Korea 2025 (n=5,251, ages 13+, face-to-face CAPI, Mar-Jul 2025) annual use: YouTube 95% (60+: 91%, up from 49% in 2020), Band 48%, Instagram 45%, TikTok 35%, Facebook 34%, KakaoStory 33%, X 14%; among users, Threads 62.2% and TikTok 52.2% use it daily or more. The same platform's reach differs by definition and provider (YouTube: 42.9M by a DataReportal-style count, 46.78M Wiseapp, 84.9% KPF, 95% Gallup), and a search summary mixed the KPF and Gallup figures, so keep each with its own source.
findings.relevance: These are `statistical` (B) bounds on who could be on a channel by age, never on who posts there. Record the survey's definition (recent vs annual use) next to any number. Shows YouTube is near-universal, Instagram is young, Band is the 50s-60s community channel.

findings.topic: Cross-platform: public measured sources usable as neutral denominators
findings.finding: Public Korean sources that can serve as denominators: MSIT/NIA 2025 Internet Usage Survey (22,671 households, 50,750 people aged 3+; internet use 95.0%; generative-AI experience 44.5%); KISDI Korea Media Panel 2025 (3,956 households, 8,411 people); KPF 2024 social media survey; Gallup Korea Market70 2025 (n=5,251). Vendor-run and therefore `estimate` (C): Nasmedia NPR 2026 (n=2,000 internet users, fielded 4-13 Feb 2026; e.g., 82.5% watch short-form daily), Opensurvey social-media report 2025 (ages 15-59, n=3,000), 대학내일20대연구소, Wiseapp. Reuters Digital News Report 2025 Korea: about 50% use YouTube for news weekly and portal (Naver) news prominence is falling.
findings.relevance: Maps to source-grading families: MSIT, KISDI, KPF and Gallup as `statistical`; Nasmedia, Opensurvey, 20slab and Wiseapp as `estimate`. Community posts and post counts must never be the denominator (source-grading section 6).

findings.topic: Cross-platform: community usage by age and sex (대학내일20대연구소)
findings.finding: 대학내일20대연구소 (a commercial youth-research firm; reports 2021 and 2023, samples of roughly 15-39/53 year olds) found 71.4% of MZ used an online community in the last month (20s 74.8%, teens 59.6%), 4.4 days a week on average; 30s were the heaviest (4.8 days, 51.4% daily). Portal cafes were the most-used community type (63.8%), with community websites, open chat and commerce communities each around 30%. Gen Z spent 86.2 min on weekdays and 89.2 on weekends. By age: 15-18 lean to Discord, Yeolpumta and Danggeun neighbourhood life; 19-24 to Everytime and DC Inside; 25-29 to Blind. Male millennials over-index on DC Inside and Nate Pann; female early millennials on Danggeun and Ohouse commerce communities. Topics: teens games, 20s daily life, 30s economy/finance.
findings.relevance: One of the few published links between named communities and age/sex, but a young, vendor-run sample. Use for segment_exists hints and channel choice (grade C), not shares.

findings.topic: Cross-platform: per-community gender/age numbers are unreliable (conflicts)
findings.finding: Similarweb pages (modelled estimates, mainly web traffic) give: dcinside.com 79.6% male, largest age 18-24 (Aug 2026); fmkorea.com 80.6% male (Apr 2026); ruliweb.com 84.7% male, 18-24; ppomppu.co.kr 76.9% male, 25-34; pann.nate.com 63.4% male, 25-34; theqoo.net 55.9% male (read from the img.theqoo.net subdomain). Those last two contradict the widely repeated female skew of theqoo and Nate Pann (a wiki cites Kakao Data Trend May 2021-May 2022 at 94% female for theqoo, ages 40s>30s>50s>20s>60s; the operator is said to claim 80-90% female), so the model is not trustworthy for female-skewed sites. Rankify age numbers for DC Inside (10s 8%, 20s 21%, 30s 29%, 40s 25%, 50s 16%) are interest-based, not user counts. Many 'community demographics' posts surfaced were themselves posts on FM Korea, Clien, DC Inside and Ruliweb.
findings.relevance: Treat every community-level gender/age figure as lead-only (D). Never use as `segment_share`. Add a rule that modelled web-traffic panels are at best `estimate` and unusable for gender/age of Korean communities.

findings.topic: DC Inside galleries: who, tone, ownership
findings.finding: Korea Herald (Feb 2025): about 3M daily users, nearly 3M posts and comments a day, 8th most-visited site in Korea; founded 1999 as a digital-camera forum; no login needed to post or comment, IP addresses shown only partially; each gallery grows its own culture, most tolerate extreme trolling and misinformation. Peer-reviewed: PLOS ONE 2024 (Koo et al.) analysed 396,496 posts/comments from 2015-2022 across Korean communities including DC Inside, FM Korea, Ruliweb, Inven, Clien, Ppomppu, Ilbe Storehouse and Humoruniv; hate speech mostly polarises on political orientation and age, and shifted over time from gender to age. Skew: Similarweb about 80% male, 18-24 largest; 20slab says 19-24 and male millennials over-index. Ownership: H Private Equity bought it for about KRW 200bn (SPA Feb 2026, closing Mar 2026); CEO stays; buyer says no real-name system and plans UI, infrastructure, app and AI search/recommendation investment.
findings.relevance: Voice source with high toxicity and sarcasm; anonymous posters count per thread (source-grading section 5). Expect policy or infrastructure changes after the sale, so re-check ToS and robots each run.

findings.topic: DC Inside: public vs gated, access, terms
findings.finding: Gallery pages are read without login (Korea Herald says even posting needs none). I found no official content API (unverified). DC Inside's published terms pages, as summarised by search, prohibit automated means (macros, bots, robots, scrapers, crawling) for using or posting content; one summary quotes a ban on crawling without prior written consent, which I could not confirm word for word. Nov 2024: minors were barred from the depression gallery (a per-gallery restriction). Which galleries need adult or member checks was not verified.
findings.relevance: Public but ToS-restricted. Route table already has gall.dcinside.com with mobile twin. Keep single honest reads after robots/ToS check, or the researcher's own browsing; consider a default `deny_hosts` suggestion for bulk work. Under Supreme Court 2021Do1533, explicit terms and technical measures are what make access unauthorised.

findings.topic: theqoo
findings.finding: Reported as a female-dominated celebrity/idol/drama community: an operator claim of 80-90% female and Kakao Data Trend (May 2021-May 2022) at 94% female with 40s>30s>50s>20s>60s and almost no teens, all via namu.wiki (user-edited, low quality); Similarweb disagrees (55.9% male on the image subdomain). Described as closed and insular, with quick swings of opinion. Access per wiki-level sources: most boards readable without login, some categories (daily-talk, dating) need login, writing and commenting need an account, and sign-ups open only in limited windows. Terms page exists at theqoo.net/service; its automated-collection clause and robots.txt were not verified. The project notes already say theqoo needs an R3 render.
findings.relevance: Female 30s-40s celebrity and lifestyle talk is a valuable segment voice but the evidence on who they are is weak; keep segment claims `lead_only`. Login-gated categories are `auth_gate` stops, not gaps to work around.

findings.topic: FM Korea (에펨코리아)
findings.finding: About 80.6% male per Similarweb (Apr 2026); Korean Wikipedia and Weekly Chosun describe mostly male users into overseas football and games, rank 6th among Korean sites and 2nd among communities in Oct 2022 (unverified). PLOS ONE 2024 places it on the conservative side (with Ilbe Storehouse; Clien on the liberal side). A DBpia study of its politics board (Apr 2021-Mar 2022) reads the 'anti-feminism' talk of young men as framed by meritocratic 'fairness'. The 포텐 (upvote) mechanism surfaces best-of posts, so what is visible is vote-selected. Its terms and integrated rules ban AI or automation for generating posts/comments and posting user lists, and registration can require phone, identity or e-mail duplicate checks to stop re-joining; a crawling clause was not confirmed.
findings.relevance: Vote-selected, politically tilted male voice; use for pain-point existence, never prevalence. Verify ToS and robots live before any read.

findings.topic: Nate Pann (네이트판)
findings.finding: Reported as a female-leaning, relatively young community with anonymous narrative posts (marriage, in-laws, romance, rumours); a wiki says posts are rarely verified and that fabricated stories ('판춘문예') are common, citing a 2015 hoax. Similarweb shows 63.4% male with 25-34 largest (contradicting the female-skew claim), and 20slab found male millennials over-index on it, so the audience is unclear. A KCI paper studies its everyday-life narratives and reader reception. Terms, robots.txt and login rules were not verified.
findings.relevance: Treat posts as first-person narrative claims that may be fiction; useful for situation and context existence, weak for pain-point prevalence. Add a `narrative_unverified` caution for this host.

findings.topic: Clien (클리앙)
findings.finding: IT, gadget and politics community; a blog says users are led by people in their 40s-50s (weak); PLOS ONE 2024 places it on the liberal side of the communities studied. Similarweb: rank about 1,334 worldwide, bounce 45%, Korea is the top country. Reading is possible without a login, while commenting requires login and e-mail verification (from Clien pages surfaced by search); boards beyond the general ones were not checked. The project notes say to use R3 render. Terms and robots.txt not verified.
findings.relevance: Older, tech-literate voice; good for adoption-barrier and device-context existence. Not a proxy for the general public.

findings.topic: Ppomppu (뽐뿌)
findings.finding: Deal-hunting community opened 2005-11-16, run by ㈜뽐뿌커뮤니케이션 (namu.wiki); Similarweb 76.9% male, 25-34 largest, 99% of traffic from Korea, about 21 pages per visit (very engaged); wiki-level sources say 40s are prominent. Included in the PLOS ONE hate-speech corpus. The adult forum needs adult verification (a community post). Deal boards carry promotional and affiliate-style content. Terms, robots.txt and other gating not verified.
findings.relevance: Price-sensitive utilitarian voice; apply the promotion and affiliate disclosure markers to deal posts before counting them as user voice.

findings.topic: Ruliweb (루리웹)
findings.finding: Gaming and anime community: Similarweb 84.7% male, 18-24 largest; fan-wiki descriptions split it into a 30s console-gamer core (many married) and a 10s to early-20s anime/otaku crowd; included in the PLOS ONE corpus. Terms, robots.txt and login gating not verified.
findings.relevance: Game and device UX pain points (controllers, launchers, store apps). Male and young-skewed; use as existence evidence only.

findings.topic: Instiz (인스티즈)
findings.finding: Described (namu, sitenow) as a teen-to-early-20s female idol/entertainment community with a large anonymous chat board; PLOS ONE initially included Instiz but dropped it because it had comparatively few hateful expressions; Similarweb ranks it 8th in Korea's social-network category. Whether reading needs login or membership, and its terms, were not verified (one result called it a members-only entertainment community, unconfirmed).
findings.relevance: Young female fandom voice, the most under-documented of the named communities; keep as lead-only until a live check confirms public access and terms.

findings.topic: Naver Cafe including parenting 'mom cafes': scale and users
findings.finding: Naver Cafe app had 9.52M monthly users in Feb 2025 (third SNS/community app, Wiseapp); portal cafes were the most-used community type in the 20slab sample (63.8%). Large parenting cafes: 맘스홀릭 베이비 (since 2003) is reported at roughly 3.2-3.4M members and a marketing page puts it and 레몬테라스 at 3.0-3.5M (unverified); press cites about 200 national and regional mom cafes used for marketing. Mom-cafe research (e.g., 220 women aged 20-40s) finds trust, information exchange and emotional support drive participation; local mom cafes are mostly women in their 30s-40s with young children (inference from these studies, no published share found).
findings.relevance: Important for family, childcare, education and local-service products. Membership counts are not segment shares. Cafe-level gating means most evidence will be a coverage gap.

findings.topic: Naver Cafe and mom cafes: tone and commercial bias
findings.finding: Press describes mom cafes as influential (lawmakers, schools and firms watch them) but also as venues for hidden marketing, fake reviews of new shops (Korea Economic Daily 2020) and boycott threats; one press summary says up to half of some cafes' members may be hidden marketers (unverified claim). KFTC's 2024 hidden-ad monitoring counted 984 suspected posts on 'other' platforms including TikTok and Naver Cafe, and the guideline in force since 2024-12-01 requires blogs and internet cafes to put the paid-relationship disclosure in the title or start of the post.
findings.relevance: Apply the promotion-disclosure markers strictly to cafe posts and to '공구' (group-buy) style threads; expect fear-appeal and pile-on dynamics. Consider a `commercial_infiltration_risk` note on this family.

findings.topic: Naver Cafe: public vs member-only, and the August 2026 notice
findings.finding: Boards are public or member-only per cafe; a member-only post can still appear by title in Naver search if search exposure is on, but its body needs membership, and some posts open only through a search-result path (third-party tip page). Whether the cafearticle API returns titles or snippets of such posts is unverified; if it does they are teasers (D). Around 2026-08-31 Naver posted a cafe notice strictly banning bulk collection of posts and comments without the consent of members and the cafe, or copying them to outside sites, naming crawlers/bots/scripts, unofficial routes and continuing after blocks; Naver said the notice is not about AI training and that it has blocked AI crawling of user content by default since last year. robots.txt blocks AI bots on blog (OpenAI, Perplexity, Google, Claude, Meta, Apple) and cafe (plus Amazon, Bing) since mid-2025.
findings.relevance: Treat member-only, membership-gated and search-path-gated posts as `auth_gate` or teaser; the researcher's own reading of a public board is the legitimate path, and a cafe manager's consent is the only route to more. route table 'naver-cafe' has no official route, which is correct.

findings.topic: Naver Blog: reach, users, commercial bias, visibility
findings.finding: Naver's 2025 blog report (via Daum News): 42.29M monthly active users; 19-34 year olds are 50% of blog-app users; Wiseapp (2022) found 20s the heaviest app users; KPF 2024: 21.7% use it as social media. Commercial bias is heavy: KFTC's monitoring of 2024 found 9,423 suspected hidden-ad blog posts (Instagram 10,195, YouTube 1,409; 22,011 suspected and 26,033 corrected posts overall; 26.5% no disclosure, 39.4% placed where hard to see, 17.3% tiny or faint), and a 체험단 ecosystem supplies sponsored posts. Post scopes are 전체공개, 이웃공개, 서로이웃공개 and 비공개, so only 전체공개 is public. Naver Blog RSS is listed in the project notes but I could not confirm it in this run.
findings.relevance: Public blog posts are strong for context of use and task narratives, weak for pain-point prevalence because of sponsorship. Check the top of each post for disclosure; the route table already has RSS and mobile twins (unverified).

findings.topic: Naver 지식iN (KnowledgeiN)
findings.finding: After 20 years it reported 32M cumulative users and 800M Q&As (2022); 56% of new users in 2022 were in their teens and 20s; an older analysis found answers written by 20s (29.0%) and 30s (23.3%) making up over half; Naver added an expert-answer service (doctors, lawyers, tax and labour advisers) and, in 2024, removed answer-adoption limits and launched AI answering ('지식이'). A wiki claims macro and generative-AI answers now flood it (unverified). It is reachable through the Search API 'kin' service (subject to the 2026 API changes).
findings.relevance: Questions show what people could not find or do; answers are mixed human, expert and AI, so tag authorship per answer. Young askers skew toward study and relationship topics.

findings.topic: Daum Cafe and the Daum spin-off
findings.finding: Daum's own help says cafe search returns only posts from public cafes; the Kakao Developers Daum Search API (web, video, image, blog, book, cafe) returns for cafes cafename, title, contents (a snippet), datetime, thumbnail and url, authenticated by a REST API key, with monthly and daily quotas that can be raised only through a partnership. Female community 여성시대 lives on Daum Cafe (cafe.daum.net/subdued20club; a wiki claims about 800,000 members). Ownership changed: Kakao transferred Daum services to AXZ on 2025-12-01; Upstage moved to acquire AXZ (Jan 2026) and AXZ renamed itself 'Daum' on 2026-07-27. I found no notice of API changes, and no reliable user counts or demographics for Daum Cafe.
findings.relevance: Add a 'daum-cafe' route (cafe.daum.net, m.cafe.daum.net; community family; public cafes only) and a Kakao discovery entry, marked unverified. Re-check Daum API terms, since the operator changed and Upstage is an AI company.

findings.topic: Blind (블라인드)
findings.finding: Verified-employee anonymous workplace community: 12M global sign-ups (Mar 2025), MAU 9.2M (Feb 2023, global); Korean users' average annual income KRW 67.1M against KRW 42.12M for Korean workers (Blind's own figures); Blind says more than 9 in 10 employees of Korea's ten largest groups are members (Jan 2025); women sign-ups grew over 10% since 2021. Wiseapp (Feb 2026) lists Blind among apps with a 30s user share of 37.1%. Company channels open once enough verified employees join. On the web, logged-out visitors can read some posts but only some topic channels are offered; the app is the full product. Blind's scraping terms were not verified.
findings.relevance: White-collar, high-income, grievance-tilted anonymous voice: excellent for B2B, HR-tech and workplace-tool pain points, unrepresentative of the public. Treat login and company channels as `auth_gate`; do not add Blind to signed-in communities without explicit authorisation.

findings.topic: Danggeun (Daangn, 당근)
findings.finding: Wiseapp: 21.85M users in Aug 2025 (21.22M in Aug 2024), about 2h40m and 177 launches per user per month; 40s are the largest age share (30.3%) versus Bunjang (20s 32.2%, 30s 25.5%) and Joonggonara (40s 29.9%); press in 2026 cites about 23M. 당근모임 passed 10M MAU in H1 2026 (20s 14%, 30s 26%, 40s 27%, 50s 23%, 60+ 8%). 20slab: teens and female early millennials over-index on the 동네생활 community. Content is hyperlocal: secondhand goods, neighbourhood chatter, local business promotion. Some 동네생활 posts have public web pages (daangn.com/kr/community/...); the app is the main surface. An official API, robots.txt and terms were not checked (search budget ran out).
findings.relevance: Add 'daangn' as a community-family route for public web pages only; neighbourhood names and nicknames are personal-data-adjacent, so scrub. K-skill's docs show it uses undocumented Remix and SSR routes for Daangn, which this skill must not copy.

findings.topic: YouTube comments: audience and bias
findings.finding: YouTube is Korea's biggest video venue: 46.78M average monthly users and the most total time in 2025 (Wiseapp), 95% annual use including 91% of people 60+ (Gallup 2025), and about 50% using it for news weekly (Reuters DNR 2025). Comments are tied to a specific video, so the commenting population is that video's audience, self-selected and shaped by ranking; commenters are not the user base. Hidden-ad monitoring by KFTC found 1,409 suspected posts on YouTube in 2024 and the 2020 Korean 'backdoor advertising' controversy led to the current disclosure rules.
findings.relevance: Good for context-of-use and device talk for products that get reviewed on YouTube. Use `video` family independence: one commenter, one unit; record which sort order was read.

findings.topic: YouTube comments: legitimate access and terms
findings.finding: Official route: YouTube Data API v3, commentThreads.list costs 1 quota unit and the default project quota is 10,000 units a day (search.list costs 100). YouTube's Terms of Service bar automated access (robots, botnets, scrapers) except public search engines following robots.txt or with written permission. The Developer Policies let API clients hold non-authorised data no longer than 30 days before refreshing or deleting, bar profiling users by protected attributes (age, race, religion, political leaning, sexual orientation, health), and allow aggregate sentiment or NLP on comments; there is a derived-metrics policy. Accredited academics can apply to the YouTube Researcher Program for larger quota. Creators' 'third-party training' setting defaults to off.
findings.relevance: The route table already has the API route with YOUTUBE_API_KEY. Add a 30-day retention clause to the run-folder rules for API data and a rule against inferring protected attributes of commenters (which persona building must respect).

findings.topic: Instagram and Threads in Korea: audience and tone
findings.finding: Instagram: 27.03M average monthly users in 2025 (Wiseapp); 80.9% of 20s and 70.7% of 30s use it (KPF 2024); it produced the most suspected hidden-ad posts (10,195 in KFTC's 2024 monitoring). Threads grew fast: 5.93M users Feb 2025 (+133% year on year, Wiseapp), about 5.43M in 2026 (doubled), 6.5M in another report, so providers disagree. Press attributes adoption among 20s-30s to a casual 반말 (informal speech) culture that Korean SNS did not have before.
findings.relevance: Informal 반말 and short posts change how sentiment and politeness markers should be read (do not read plain speech as rudeness). Instagram evidence is commercial-heavy.

findings.topic: Instagram and Threads: legitimate access and terms
findings.finding: Meta's Automated Data Collection Terms (effective 2024-10-07) forbid scrapers, bots and crawlers without Meta's written permission, on public pages as well. Official routes: Instagram Graph API (Business or Creator account; hashtag search limited to 30 unique hashtags per rolling 7 days and recent media from the last 24 hours); Threads API keyword search needs the threads_keyword_search permission through Meta App Review (unapproved apps only search the user's own posts; quoted rate limits conflict between sources: 2,200 per 24h vs 500 per 7 days); Meta Content Library and API for qualified academic or non-profit researchers via ICPSR (review of about 2-6 weeks; covers public Facebook, Instagram and Threads content in the UI). Whether Instagram or Threads pages show content to logged-out visitors was not verified.
findings.relevance: Treat Instagram and Threads as out of reach for the reader by default; document them as 'official route needs approval' rather than as a gap of effort. An academic partner could use Meta Content Library.

findings.topic: App store reviews in Korea: audience skew and review bombing
findings.finding: Gallup Korea 2025: main smartphone Samsung 72%, Apple 24%; 20s use Apple more than Samsung (60% vs 40%), 30s split 50/47, 50s 89% and 60+ 92% Samsung; women 27% Apple vs men 21%. So App Store reviews tilt young and female, Google Play reviews older and male. Reviews are event-driven: after KakaoTalk's 2025-09-23 redesign, its rating fell to about 1.9 on the App Store and 1.1 then 1.0 on Google Play, with 98.11% of about 3.18M raters giving 1 star by 2025-10-02; complaints were 42% general, 19% UI/design and 10% friend list/profile.
findings.relevance: Segment app-review evidence by store, country and date window, and flag redesign or outage periods; a review-bomb window is context, not a usability finding. `stale` and per-window handling matter here.

findings.topic: App Store and Google Play reviews: legitimate feeds and limits
findings.finding: App Store: the public iTunes customer-reviews RSS feed (https://itunes.apple.com/kr/rss/customerreviews/page=N/id=APPID/sortby=mostrecent/json) returns 50 reviews a page and stops at 10 pages, so at most the 500 most recent reviews per storefront; it works without a key but I found no formal Apple documentation (community and developer posts only), and it appeared still working in mid-2026 per one post. Google Play: the Play Developer API reviews.list works only for your own app, returns only reviews created or modified in the last week and only those with comments; longer history comes from a Play Console CSV export. The Play comment-posting policy says Google pays for no reviews. A public Play page shows reviews but only the first ones without interaction.
findings.relevance: App Store feed suits the R0 route in the route table; for Play use the team's own console export as `team_provided`. Record the storefront (kr) and the 500-review ceiling as coverage limits. ONE store and Galaxy Store reviews are uncovered.

findings.topic: Naver Place reviews
findings.finding: Naver Map had 30.44M monthly users in 2025 and is the top navigation app for 20s. Place reviews are tied to a visit: receipt, reservation, location and real-name checks were tightened in Oct 2024 and again from 2025-05-12 (Naver POS linkage; agencies had been farming fake and duplicate reviews). Star ratings were removed in Oct 2021 and came back on 2026-04-06 (about 4 years 9 months later); average stars and per-reviewer average stars became public on 2026-07-09; the April policy adds a banned act of giving under-3 stars indiscriminately, and shop owners fear review attacks. There is no documented review endpoint: Naver's Local Search API returns place data (sort options random or comment, i.e., review count).
findings.relevance: Reviews before April 2026 have no star score, so ratings and text cannot be compared across that date. Read only as the researcher's own browsing or the business's own Smart Place tools; note reviewer average stars as a weighting cue for the user rather than an evidence grade.

findings.topic: Kakao Map reviews
findings.finding: After a March 2025 web overhaul Kakao Map's web version dropped its '맛집' rating view and users complained; video reviews were added in May 2025 to compete with Google Maps. Users have seen it as less ad-driven than Naver (weak, wiki-level). The Kakao Local API returns place information and a place_url to the map page; the pages I could see list no review fields (unverified negative). A Kakao DevTalk thread asks whether Local API results may be stored, sent to an LLM or shown with attribution and I saw no official answer.
findings.relevance: Kakao Map review text is a gap for the reader; treat schema changes in 2025 as discontinuities. Do not send Kakao Local results to an LLM until Kakao's position is confirmed.

findings.topic: Coupang reviews: audience, bias, manipulation
findings.finding: Coupang: 33.88M average monthly users in 2025 (Wiseapp), roughly a third of the population's phones. KFTC (Aug 2024) fined Coupang and CPLB a record KRW 162.8bn for manipulating search ranking to favour its own-brand products and for using about 2,000 employees to post about 70,000 reviews on those products; Coupang sued and a court suspended the sanction in Oct 2024 (litigation ongoing). Press documents review incentives (Coupang cash, points, coupons), paid-review agencies, family-account reviews by shop owners, and 'review part-time' and fake 'Coupang partner' scams that harmed hundreds of victims. Coupang Partners footers ('쿠팡 파트너스 활동의 일환으로') are affiliate disclosures.
findings.relevance: Coupang reviews are convenience-sample and manipulable; grade as `voice` with a promotion-risk downgrade and never as prevalence. Existing markers already include the Partners disclosure phrase.

findings.topic: Coupang reviews: access and terms
findings.finding: A marketing-blog analysis says that as of 2026-09-02 Coupang's robots.txt allows search-engine bots on /vp/products/ and /np/categories/ and blocks AI crawlers (OpenAI GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User); Coupang and Naver Shopping both close the door to AI bots. Search summaries say Coupang's terms restrict automated tools. The Coupang Partners Open API is for affiliates and has no review endpoint that I could find (K-skill's docs only mention its HMAC signing). Bot-protection on the site is commonly discussed; I did not research or record ways around it. Seller-side review views for one's own products exist (unverified).
findings.relevance: Expect the reader to end at `opted_out` for coupang.com (robots.txt not allowing our token). Then use the team's own seller export as `team_provided`, or the researcher's own notes; do not route around it.

findings.topic: Naver Search API moved to NAVER API HUB (time-sensitive)
findings.finding: Naver Developers announced ([중요] Search API, Search Trend, Shopping Insight 서비스 종료 및 NAVER API HUB 이관 안내): NAVER API HUB (run through Naver Cloud Platform, pay-as-you-go with a free tier) launched 2026-06-25; new key issuance on Naver Developers stopped 2026-07-31; keys issued before about 2026-07-25 keep working until 2027-06-30, after which calls are blocked; the shopping, book and professional-document search APIs ended 2026-07-31. New endpoints are naverapihub.apigw.ntruss.com/search/v1/{blog|news|local|...} with headers X-NCP-APIGW-API-KEY-ID and X-NCP-APIGW-API-KEY instead of openapi.naver.com and X-Naver-Client-Id/Secret; parameters and response formats are said to be unchanged. Reported free quota is 25,000 calls a day (775,000 a month) per search API, excess price not fixed.
findings.relevance: The skill's routes.json discovery entry 'naver-search-open-api' (openapi.naver.com, NAVER_CLIENT_ID/SECRET) is now legacy: no new keys, ends 2027-06-30. Update endpoints, env names and docs, and note that a Naver Cloud account is now needed.

findings.topic: Naver Search API terms: AI-input ban and no-storage (time-sensitive, most important terms finding)
findings.finding: Naver's revised 'search API special terms' in the NAVER API service terms took effect 2026-09-07 (announced early Aug 2026). As reported by TokenPost, Data Economy, Newsway and Digital Today: the Search API may be used only to show Naver search results in an application; inputting API data into AI or using it to train, improve, evaluate or 'expose' AI is banned (press reads this as closing RAG/LLM answers too); copying or storing the data, giving or selling it to third parties, ads on pages showing results and separate monetisation are also banned. Earlier NCP 'AI-NAVER API service terms' (2021 PDF, quoted in a GitHub issue) already said API results must not be stored separately or made into a database. I did not open Naver's official notice, so the exact wording is unverified.
findings.relevance: Direct conflict with an LLM agent reading API snippets and with the run folder saving text. Recommend: do not feed Naver API results to a model; switch the discovery entry off by default, or limit it to a human-only link list, until the official text is read. Add a per-host flag such as `ai_input_forbidden` to the brief's access policy.

findings.topic: Naver general terms, robots.txt and AI-bot blocking
findings.finding: Naver's terms say the databases built with Naver services are protected by measures such as robots.txt and that collecting robots.txt-protected databases with any robot other than Naver's is not allowed (quoted by Nate News and The Public in the Oct 2024 debate over Naver's AI-training clause in its terms). A forum answer gives www.naver.com/robots.txt as 'User-agent: * / Disallow: / / Allow: /$' (unverified; I could not fetch it). Since June-July 2025 Naver applies robots.txt blocks for AI crawlers on all services (GPTBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended and others per press) and blog pages carry anti-crawling code. Automated login is a terms violation.
findings.relevance: For naver.com hosts the reader's robots check will most likely end in `opted_out`, so Naver blog, cafe and 지식iN content comes from the researcher's own reading or nothing. Say so in the access table rather than climbing rungs.

findings.topic: Naver Search API official spec (from Naver's GitHub)
findings.finding: The official swagger (github.com/naver/naver-openapi-guide) lists search services at /v1/search/{service} for blog, news, book, encyc, cafearticle, kin, webkr, image, shop, doc, adult and errata; parameters query (UTF-8), display 10-100 (default 10), start 1-1000 (default 1), sort sim or date (not for encyc, webkr, doc); local search at /v1/search/local with sort random or comment (review count); auth headers X-Naver-Client-Id and X-Naver-Client-Secret; terms link developers.naver.com/products/terms. The swagger has no response schemas and no quota text. The apilist also shows a login-based Cafe API for joining and posting (not for reading). A user-verified issue states the binding limit is start<=1000, so one query can never return more than 1,000 items.
findings.relevance: Query splitting, not quota, limits coverage; results are titles, snippets and links (D). Plan any discovery around the 1,000-result cap, and keep it lead-only.

findings.topic: Naver DataLab: official aggregated interest by gender and age
findings.finding: The official swagger shows the DataLab search-trend API takes startDate (from 2016-01-01), endDate, timeUnit (date, week, month), up to 5 keywordGroups of up to 20 keywords, and optional device (pc or mo), gender (m or f) and ages (buckets 1-11); it returns a relative search-volume index. It moved to NAVER API HUB with the search API. One issue reports 50,000 calls a month per DataLab category (unverified). Whether the September 2026 AI restrictions cover DataLab was not confirmed.
findings.relevance: A legitimate official route to 'who searches for this' by gender and age that touches no posts (grade C estimate of interest, not of users). Check its terms before letting an agent read responses.

findings.topic: Kakao Daum Search API and Kakao Developers policy
findings.finding: Kakao Developers applies monthly and daily quotas; the Daum search endpoints (web, video, image, blog, book, cafe) use 'Authorization: KakaoAK REST_API_KEY' at dapi.kakao.com/v2/search/...; quota increases need a partnership proposal. A Kakao DevTalk thread quotes item 20 of Article 5 of the operating policy as forbidding caching Kakao data, or keeping the cache current, for purposes other than improving the in-app user experience. Several developers asked whether results may be stored, filtered, or passed to an external LLM (threads 150751, 151458, 151545, 151660) and I saw no official answer. The per-day quota number is unconfirmed.
findings.relevance: Do not treat Daum API text as storable or LLM-safe: keep API results as ephemeral leads until Kakao's answer is found. Use env KAKAO_REST_API_KEY only from the user's own key.

findings.topic: Law: Supreme Court 2021Do1533 (crawling)
findings.finding: On 2022-05-12 the Supreme Court (2021Do1533, Yanolja v. Goodchoice) confirmed acquittal of a company that crawled a competitor's app API server, on charges under the Network Act (unauthorised access, Art. 48), the Copyright Act (database-maker right, Art. 93) and computer-obstruction of business. It held that whether access is restricted is judged from objectively revealed circumstances such as protective measures and terms of use, not the provider's subjective wish; here the API was reachable through the public app and the terms did not forbid crawling or packet capture. It is the first Supreme Court crawling ruling. Explicit terms and technical barriers therefore raise risk.
findings.relevance: Supports the skill's stance: stop at technical controls, robots.txt and explicit terms; where terms forbid automated collection the risk is real. This is not legal advice and a criminal acquittal does not clear civil liability.

findings.topic: Law: civil liability and database rights despite criminal acquittal
findings.finding: The same Yanolja v. Goodchoice dispute went civil: the Seoul Central District Court ordered KRW 1bn under the Unfair Competition Prevention Act (unfair use of another's investment, '성과 도용') at first instance. In Saramin v. JobKorea the appeal court held crawling job postings infringed JobKorea's database-maker right under Copyright Act Art. 93(1)-(2), awarding KRW 250M plus indirect compulsion (about KRW 450M in total), and the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal without full review. Also relevant in Korea: Network Act Art. 48 (exceeding permitted access) and Copyright Act Art. 93.
findings.relevance: Bulk or systematic copying of a site's data is the risky pattern, matching the skill's per-host caps and the 'no database building' rule. Keep excerpts short and per-person caps.

findings.topic: Law and regulator guidance: personal data and AI
findings.finding: PIPC's guide on publicly available personal information for AI development and services (2024-07-17) treats web data (websites, blogs) as personal information whose collection and use is 'processing' under PIPA, allows processing on the 'legitimate interests' basis when three conditions are met, and expects safeguards. The Ministry of Culture and the Korea Copyright Commission published a non-binding guide on fair use for generative-AI training (2026-02-26) built on the four factors of Copyright Act Art. 35-5(2). Neither opens a right to bypass a site's terms.
findings.relevance: Supports the skill's pseudonymous author keys, no profiles of individuals, short excerpts and scrubbed segment summaries. Add PIPA and the PIPC guide to the responsibility section next to Art. 48 and Art. 93.

findings.topic: Regulation: KFTC endorsement disclosure and Korean review culture ('내돈내산')
