findings.finding: KFTC's revised guideline on recommendations and endorsements took effect 2024-12-01: for text media such as blogs and internet cafes the paid or in-kind relationship must appear in the title or opening of the post, in plain wording, and conditional phrases like 'may receive a fee' do not count. Vague labels such as 체험단, 선물, 숙제 and 서포터스 are not accepted as disclosure; the term 협찬 for free goods and 광고 for paid ads are expected. KFTC's 2024 monitoring: 22,011 suspected hidden-ad posts, 26,033 corrected; 39.4% placed in hard-to-see spots, 26.5% undisclosed. Posts claiming '내돈내산' (bought with my own money) were a common cover for sponsored content, and contracts must be disclosed even then.
findings.relevance: Add a placement check (title or first lines) to the promotion grading, and treat '내돈내산' as neither a disclosure nor proof of independence. The existing 체험단 and 서포터즈 markers stay as promotion signals.

findings.topic: K-skill: how a Korean agent-skill repo is organised
findings.finding: NomaDamas/k-skill (MIT) has 125+ skills in about 19 life-domain groups (transport, real estate, law, tax, jobs, finance, health, shopping, food, sport, culture, education, news, Korean language, weather, lifestyle, developer tools, fortune) plus k-skill-setup and k-skill-cleaner. Each skill needs skill.json (name, description, profiles, frontmatter), instruction.md and a generated SKILL.md adapter; kebab-case names equal to the folder; frontmatter name, description, license and metadata.category/locale/phase (locale ko-KR); a docs/features/<skill>.md page; tests; `npm run ci` validation. Secrets follow KSKILL_<SERVICE>_<ITEM>; credential order is host vault or injected env, then agent vault, then ~/.config/k-skill/secrets.env (mode 0600); the model never reads secret values. Docs include security-and-secrets, sources.md (narrative per-source access notes with dated live checks), legal/ (read-only skill risk resolution, trademark review), a roadmap with an 'On Hold' list and reasons, and an optional hosted proxy for public government APIs with a privacy notice. Rule: official APIs first, then public JSON/RSS/sitemap/mobile pages, browser only as a fallback, and never bypass CAPTCHA or authentication.
findings.relevance: Borrow: locale and category metadata, a dated per-source access log, an On Hold list with reasons, the credential-resolution order, a legal note structured by statute (Copyright Act 91-93, Network Act 48, PIPA 3) with seven re-review triggers, and a required attribution of source URL and author in outputs. Do not borrow the proxy that injects the operator's keys.

findings.topic: K-skill: where its research approach conflicts with this skill's rules
findings.finding: K-skill's naver-blog-research works 'without an API key' by loading Naver's search result pages (search.naver.com/search.naver?where=blog) and reading posts from m.blog.naver.com; its docs warn bulk use risks IP blocking and limit it to small, non-commercial personal lookup. Its docs/sources.md also documents undocumented surfaces (Naver Shopping public BFF JSON, Daangn Remix data routes and SSR store parsing, Kakao Places panel JSON). Naver's terms and robots.txt, the August 2026 cafe notice and the September 2026 API terms all cut against this pattern, and this skill forbids scraping search-result pages and calling undocumented endpoints.
findings.relevance: Do not port those routes. Keep the reader ladder honest: official routes, the site's own public pages, the researcher's own browsing. Note the k-skill precedent only as an ecosystem contrast.

findings.topic: Audiences that sit in member-only venues (outside the public reader)
findings.finding: Key Korean audiences gather where the reader cannot go: Everytime (campus community; 77.5% of its app users are in their 20s per Wiseapp, 19-24 year olds per 20slab), Band (used by 48% annually per Gallup, and by 40.6% of 50s and 31.1% of 60s per KPF), KakaoTalk open chat and Discord (teens per 20slab), and closed cafes. The route table already lists band.us, open.kakao.com and Discord as out of scope.
findings.relevance: Say explicitly in reports that 50s-60s and student segments are under-covered by the public web; use survey or interview routes for them instead of forum text.

findings.topic: Synthesis: access verdict by platform (inference from the findings above)
findings.finding: Official route an agent can use with the user's own key or approval: YouTube Data API (comments), Google Play (own app only), the public App Store RSS feed (500 most recent per storefront; formal terms unverified), Threads keyword search and Instagram Graph (after Meta approval), Meta Content Library (academic/non-profit). Official route exists but its terms now conflict with an AI agent reading it: Naver Search API for blog, cafe and 지식iN (from 2026-09-07), Daum Search API (caching and LLM questions unanswered). findings.topic: T1-1 language | Slang lexicon: no single authority, vocabulary drifts
findings.finding: There is no authoritative slang list. 국립국어원 publishes periodic 신어 자료집 (2003, 2009, 2017, 2018, 2019 ...) and states that survey methods miss many neologisms and that a listed word is neither approved as standard nor recommended. 우리말샘 (opendict.korean.go.kr) is an open dictionary of about 1 million entries (표준국어대사전 plus roughly 500,000 neologisms, everyday, dialect and technical terms) that users propose and editors review; 표준국어대사전 has an Open API on data.go.kr (data/3057780). KoNeoBench (arXiv 2609.19916, Sept 2026) is a new benchmark of LLM understanding of 1,785 neologisms attested in online news since 2020 (recognition, source-component recovery, categorisation, definition generation); its results were not read.
findings.relevance: research-protocol.md 'Query expansion' already says to add terms found in user language. Make that operational for Korean: keep a dated, per-community expansion list (term, spelling variants, first seen, example URL) instead of a static slang table; look a token up in 우리말샘 before interpreting it; never let a model assert a slang meaning without a corpus example; do not present dictionary entries as usage frequency.

findings.topic: T1-2 language | 초성체 (initial-consonant writing): what it is and how far to trust a reading
findings.finding: 초성체 writes a word by its initial consonants only (ㅇㅈ, ㄱㅅ, ㅊㅅㅊ, ㅋㅋ). Encyclopedia and linguistics sources describe it as growing out of laughter onomatopoeia (ㅋㅋ, ㅎㅎ) and spreading with 1990s PC-communication chat as shorthand or as an allusive way to write ordinary words; 통신언어 surveys (이정복 in 새국어생활 2003; a Kyung Hee ISLI paper) document its spelling and sound features. Such strings are ambiguous by design: one string can stand for several words and the positive or negative sense depends on the thread. I found no authoritative decoding table. 'OKIWI 초성체 해석기' (bab2min) is a community research aid that proposes readings.
findings.relevance: In captures keep the raw string; expand only with readings supported by the same thread; when a 초성 token carries the sentiment or the claim, record polarity as unknown and never let a 초성-only post support a claim alone. Spelling out the word and adding the 초성 form in queries can widen recall but the 초성 form has low precision.

findings.topic: T1-3 language | Unicode: syllables, jamo, compatibility jamo, NFC/NFD
findings.finding: Modern Hangul syllables are precomposed code points U+AC00-U+D7A3 (11,172 assigned). Conjoining jamo sit in U+1100-U+11FF. The 'compatibility jamo' U+3130-U+318F (ㄱ U+3131, ㅋ U+314B ...) are standalone letters kept for KS X 1001 compatibility; ㅋㅋ, ㅠㅠ and 초성 strings are written in this block. NFC composes jamo sequences into syllables; NFD/NFKD decompose syllables into conjoining jamo, so identical-looking Korean can differ at code-point level (macOS file names, some editors, copy-paste). A public issue report shows a Korean search library failing to derive 초성 from NFD text (croco-dev/framework #2987).
findings.relevance: Reader/extractor and marker matching: normalise page text, queries and marker lists to NFC before matching; derive 초성 or jamo only from NFC input; treat runs of compatibility jamo (ㅋㅋㅋ, ㅎㅎ, ㅠㅠ, ㅇㅇ) as tokens, not noise; add NFD test cases for uxresearch/data/markers.json (privacy.py already imports unicodedata).

findings.topic: T1-4 language | 야민정음 and look-alike spellings
findings.finding: 야민정음 (野民正音) rewrites syllables with look-alike glyphs (멍멍이->댕댕이, 귀여워->커여워, 명곡->띵곡, 팔도 비빔면->괄도 네넴띤). The name comes from DCInside's domestic-baseball gallery ('야갤') plus 훈민정음, where it developed, and it later spread; a 2022 Hangul-day event by 국립국어원 about it drew criticism. Related 통신체/급식체 spellings break spacing and spelling rules on purpose. Readers can usually recover the intended word, so these are wordplay, not errors, but they defeat exact-match search.
findings.relevance: Query expansion: for each core term add look-alike and phonetic variants actually seen in the corpus (do not generate them blindly); count a variant spelling as the same word when judging independent voices; keep the original spelling in excerpts.

findings.topic: T1-5 language | Consumer and rating slang seen in reviews
findings.finding: Press and encyclopedic sources: 혜자 (great value for the price, from actress 김혜자 who fronted a convenience-store lunch box) and 창렬 (poor value or over-packaged, from singer 김창렬's branded chilled foods) are opposite value-for-money words reported in 2015. 내돈내산 ('bought with my own money') signals a review is not sponsored and spread after the 2020 뒷광고 controversy. 상타취/ㅅㅌㅊ (above average) and 하타취/ㅎㅌㅊ (below average) with 평타(취) as the middle (there is no '중타취') reportedly began in 2011 on the site 일베저장소 and are now used across many communities; some users object to them as demeaning. I found no dictionary source for these.
findings.relevance: Seed the lexicon with value and quality vocabulary, each flagged 'press-sourced, not dictionary-verified'. Treat 상타취/하타취 as informal ratings and do not infer a poster's community or politics from the word. Keep 내돈내산 as a self-declared claim (see T2-10).

findings.topic: T1-6 language | Community identity jargon that affects independence counting (DCInside, 뽐뿌)
findings.finding: DCInside has three poster types: 유동닉 (not logged in, anonymous), 고정닉 (logged in with a nickname checked to be unique) and 반고정닉 (logged in but nickname not uniqueness-checked; the default after sign-up). Most 반고닉 use the same default nickname 'ㅇㅇ' as 유동닉, so 'ㅇㅇ' is not an identity. 뽐뿌 (Ppomppu) names both the deal community and the urge to buy at the sight of a good price; Clien, Ruliweb, FMKorea and theqoo host similar deal and review boards (definitions of 지름/눈팅/인증 were not confirmed).
findings.relevance: Supports the existing rule 'anonymous posters count by thread': never make an author key from the handle 'ㅇㅇ' on DCInside, and treat 반고닉 with 'ㅇㅇ' the same as 유동. Hot-deal boards are a place where affiliate links are common (not verified here), so run the promotion check on them.

findings.topic: T1-7 language | Reading sarcasm and irony (반어, 비꼼)
findings.finding: Korean irony is realised at phonological, inflectional, lexical, syntactic and pragmatic levels, usually by several cues together; in text the prosodic layer (intonation, pitch, stress, pause, length) is lost, which is why written sarcasm is hard to read (강원대 인문과학연구소 paper on 한국어 반어법의 실현방법). KoCoSa (LREC-COLING 2024) is a 12.8K-dialogue Korean sarcasm set: dialogues were generated from source dialogues by LLMs, filtered and human-annotated; a fine-tuned baseline beat GPT-3.5, detection depended on having enough dialogue context, and Korean sarcasm research is thinner than for other languages. Design guidance (mine, unvalidated): read sarcasm only with the parent post and neighbouring replies; flag 'polarity uncertain' when praise sits next to a laugh marker (ㅋㅋ/ㅎㅎ), a tilde or ellipsis, quotation marks, an abrupt switch between 해요체/합쇼체 and 반말, or when the reported outcome contradicts the praise; never count an uncertain post toward a satisfaction or preference claim.
findings.relevance: evidence-classification.md: add 'sarcasm risk' to the Low level of the confidence rubric, require the verifier to read the thread, and keep sentiment an inference label. KoCoSa's dialogues are synthetic, so it supports 'context matters', not the precision of any marker list.

findings.topic: T1-8 language | Honorific levels and register as context cues
findings.finding: 국립국어원 (표준국어대사전 and its online Q&A) classifies 상대 높임법 into 격식체 (하십시오체, 하오체, 하게체, 해라체) and 비격식체 (해요체, 해체 = 반말). Register therefore carries setting and stance: official notices, ads and customer-service replies use 합쇼체 (-습니다) or polite 해요체; reviews and blogs mostly 해요체 or plain -다; anonymous peer boards often use 해체/반말 (my observation, unsourced). Register shows the setting and the writer's stance, not the writer's age or gender.
findings.relevance: extract.py/verdict.py already use 해요체 vs -다 vs -니다 to tell posts from site notices. Extend to: a register shift inside a reply chain as an irritation or sarcasm flag; formal 합쇼체 inside a 'review' as a weak promotional-copy cue. Never infer demographics from register or address terms (형, 언니, 님): condition and segment shares need measured sources (source-grading.md section 3).

findings.topic: T1-9 language | Evidential endings help separate firsthand from secondhand
findings.finding: Korean marks the source of the speaker's knowledge in verb endings. Linguistics papers treat retrospective -더- (-더라, -더니) as tying a statement to what the speaker perceived (speaker, past, perception); reportative endings such as -대/-래/-라더라/-라고 하던데 and phrases like '들었는데' or '지인이 그러는데' present hearsay; '카더라' is the joking name for rumour. Casual writing uses these more loosely than textbook rules.
findings.relevance: The capture record has 'Firsthand / secondhand / unclear' and source-grading.md section 4 lowers secondhand claims one grade. Add Korean cue lists (hearsay endings, 들었는데, ~라더라) as weak signals that route a post to the verifier, not as automatic downgrades; -더라 is not proof of firsthand use.

findings.topic: T1-10 language | Official Korean search APIs the skill can use with the user's own key (docs read)
findings.finding: Naver Search API docs (vendor repo naver/naver-openapi-guide, files byte-identical to the copies read): the search API's daily limit is 25,000 calls; it is a non-login API using X-Naver-Client-Id/-Secret headers. Blog search returns title, link, description (a passage with <b> tags), bloggername, bloggerlink, postdate; cafearticle returns title, link, description, cafename, cafeurl and covers public cafe boards only; parameters query, display (max 100), start (max 1000), sort (sim or date), so at most 1,000 hits per query. The errata endpoint converts text typed in the wrong 한/영 state (docs example: spdlqj -> 네이버). The DataLab search-trend API allows 1,000 calls per day, dates from 2016-01-01, and returns a relative ratio (largest value in the result = 100) that can be split by device (pc/mo), gender and age band. Kakao's Daum Search REST API covers web, video, image, blog, book and cafe under monthly and daily quotas (numbers not verified).
findings.relevance: public-page-access.md section 15 lists RSS and mobile twins for Naver blog and cafe but not the search API; add Naver and Kakao search APIs as R0 discovery routes (key from an environment variable). Results are snippets, so they are leads (grade D) until the page is read through the reader; the 1,000-hit cap means many narrow queries, not deep paging. DataLab is an interest index, never a size (source-grading.md section 6). Use errata to repair mistyped Latin-layout queries. Terms of use for storing API results were not read.

findings.topic: T1-11 language | Portal search operators are not Google's
findings.finding: User guides say Naver's basic operators are + (must include), - (exclude), quotation marks (exact phrase) and | (or); I could not confirm site:, before: or after: operators on Naver (unverified), and the official Naver help page was not readable. research-protocol.md's advice to vary site:, OR, after: and before: assumes Google-style operators.
findings.relevance: For Korean portals plan queries around +, -, quotes and | and put date limits in the API's sort/date parameters or in the query wording (year, version, '업데이트 후'), not in operators. Treat operator behaviour as 'verify live' in the channel notes.

findings.topic: T2-1 promotion | KFTC 추천·보증 등에 관한 표시·광고 심사지침, current text (예규 제499호, issued and effective 2026-06-01; read in full)
findings.finding: Core rules: if the endorser receives cash, the product, vouchers, points, discounts, or is employed by the advertiser, the economic interest must be disclosed 'for every single post' (매 건마다); examples needing disclosure include an employee of the advertiser or its agency posting a recommendation on a blog, cafe, SNS or portal Q&A; no disclosure is needed where the benefit does not affect credibility (a sample given to all applicants, a keepsake given to all event participants). Four principles: placed next to the content (not in comments, not behind '더보기', not buried mid-text); recognisable (size, colour, contrast, speech speed); clear; same language as the post. Per medium: text posts (blog, cafe) - title or first part, larger or differently coloured; photos - text inside the picture, or first line, or first hashtag; video - title, or in-video at start and end and repeated (example: every 5 minutes); live - repeated. Clear wordings: '#광고', '#협찬', '광고입니다', '[광고] ... 솔직 사용 후기', '소정의 원고료를 지급받았지만 ...', '소정의 수수료를 지급받음', '협찬받음', '유료 광고', '경제적 대가(현금, 상품권, 수수료, 포인트, 무료 상품 등)를 받았음', '무료 상품', '상품 협찬', '상품 할인'. NOT clear: '체험 후기', '일주일 동안 사용해 보았음', '체험단', '이 글은 정보/홍보성 글임', '선물', '~에서 보내주셨어요', '#[브랜드명]', '[브랜드]x[계정]', unclear abbreviations, and foreign labels ('Advertisement', 'AD', 'PR', 'Collaboration', 'Partnership', 'Sponsor', 'spon', 'sp', 'Collabo', 'Thanks to', 'Ambassador'). New item V.5 (2026-06-01): an AI-generated 'virtual person' giving an endorsement must be disclosed as such near the person or in the title or first part. A testimonial from someone who never used the product ('이용후기 또는 사진을 올려 마치 실제 사용한 것처럼') is itself listed as an unfair ad, and the advertiser bears the burden of proving endorsement content.
findings.relevance: (a) '체험단' alone is not a compliant disclosure but is still a strong promotion signal for grading (cap D). (b) A disclosure may sit in an image, a hashtag, a comment or behind '더보기', and platform-native banners may not be in extracted text, so a text-only reader must record 'no disclosure found' as unknown, not as organic. (c) uxresearch/data/markers.json promotion.ko lacks several KFTC-clear forms: '광고입니다', '협찬 광고', '대가성 광고', '경제적 대가', '금전적 지원', '무료 상품', '상품 협찬', '협찬받음', '광고료', '대가로 작성', '가상인물 포함'; add 'AD/PR/Sponsor/Collabo/Ambassador' only as weak signals in the title, first line or first hashtag. (d) The regulator's own examples of fabricated first-hand posts are the definition of astroturf to use in grading.

findings.topic: T2-2 promotion | Legal hooks: 표시광고법, KFTC deceptive-ad and internet-ad guidelines
findings.finding: 표시ㆍ광고의 공정화에 관한 법률 (Act 20712, 2025-01-21): 3(1) forbids 사업자등 to make, or to make others make, false or exaggerated, deceptive (기만적), unfairly comparative or disparaging ads that may harm fair trade; 시행령 3(2): deceptive = 사실을 은폐하거나 축소하는 등의 방법; 17: up to 2 years or 150 million won; 9: surcharge up to 2% of turnover (500 million won if no turnover). KFTC 기만적인 표시·광고 심사지침 (예규 제488호, 2025-10-30) lists '경제적 이해관계 존재 사실의 은폐 또는 누락' with examples: an agency pays influencers without clear disclosure; an advertiser's employee recommends a product in a major online community without saying so; an advertiser posts on its own SNS account as if a third party recommended. KFTC 인터넷 광고에 관한 심사지침 (예규 제272호, 2016-12-23): a business that deletes or hides unfavourable consumer reviews on its own site without reasonable cause may be committing unfair advertising. The Act's addressee is the business and whoever it causes to advertise, not the ordinary poster.
findings.relevance: source-grading.md section 4 has 'promotion or affiliate disclosure -> at most D'. Add two Korean grounds from these texts: (i) staff or agency posts in communities are concealed interest even when no word like 협찬 appears; (ii) a brand's own review board is curated by the brand, so missing complaints there say little (see T2-8). Never label a named person an advertiser; record a promotion signal with the marker and its location.

findings.topic: T2-3 promotion | How old is the disclosure convention? Revision timeline
findings.finding: KFTC press releases and law-firm notes: comprehensive revision effective 2020-09-01 (economic-interest disclosure principles and per-medium methods for YouTube, Instagram and others, after the 2020 뒷광고 controversy); revision effective 2024-12-01 (text media such as blogs and cafes: disclosure in the title or first part; secondary reports also say conditional wording like '소정의 수수료를 지급받을 수 있음' is treated as unclear, but the current guideline text I read does not list that phrase, so it may come from the Q&A guide or the notice text); the Q&A guide '추천보증심사지침 안내서: Q&A로 알아보는 경제적 이해관계 표시' (25 questions) was revised again around 2025-12-02; 2026-04-08 notice and 2026-06-01 entry into force of the AI virtual-person rule.
findings.relevance: Grade a post against the convention of its date: before 2020-09-01 there was no per-medium rule (pre-2020 versions not read) and before 2024-12-01 the 'first part of a blog post' placement was not required, so a missing top-of-post disclosure in older posts says less. Record published_at for every promotion judgment (valid_at logic already in source-grading.md).

findings.topic: T2-4 promotion | KFTC monitoring counts and cases (regulator-documented, not prevalence)
findings.finding: KFTC SNS monitoring: March-December 2023 found 25,966 suspected posts and 29,792 were corrected (reported 2024-08); 2024 found 22,011 suspected posts - Instagram 10,195, Naver Blog 9,423, YouTube 1,409, other platforms such as TikTok and Naver Cafe 984 (the four add up to 22,011) - and 26,033 corrected (reported 2025-03-14); main defects were wrong placement and unclear wording of disclosures. First influencer-ad sanction: 2019-11-26, seven businesses, 269 million won in total. 2024-07-24: agencies 마켓잇 (Instagram, 3,944 posts for 267 advertisers, 2022-10-15 to 2023-10-03) and 플로우마케팅 (Naver blog posts, 2,653 for 88 advertisers, 2021-01-04 to 2023-12-31, influencers posting pre-written ad text) received correction and publication orders and 1 million won fines for presenting paid posts as first-hand experience.
findings.relevance: Regulator-documented facts that undisclosed paid posts occur on Instagram and Naver Blog and that agencies supply the text (supports the 'identical text counts once, flagged copypaste' rule in source-grading.md section 4). These are counts of suspicious posts found by KFTC monitoring, not a prevalence estimate: never use them as a denominator or as a share of posts that are ads.

findings.topic: T2-5 promotion | Platform staff reviews on a marketplace (Coupang, KFTC 2024)
findings.finding: KFTC decision 의결2024-284 (2024-08-05): Coupang was fined about 162.8 billion won (announced in June 2024 as 140 billion) for manipulating search rankings of its own-brand products and for using employees' reviews; reports say about 2,000 employees were given free own-brand products and asked to leave high ratings and reviews. Coupang challenged the decision in court; the outcome was not verified.
findings.relevance: First-party and platform-staff reviews are a documented astroturf mechanism on Korean marketplaces: treat ratings and top reviews of a platform's own-brand items as promotion-adjacent voice (cap D) unless corroborated on an independent channel.

findings.topic: T2-6 promotion | Review events inflate star ratings on delivery apps (KCA 2024)
findings.finding: Korea Consumer Agency study of the review systems of Baemin, Coupang Eats and Yogiyo (announced 2024-07-23): 77.3% of surveyed users wrote a review after ordering and 65.2% of those wrote it to join a 'review event' (points or gifts); the press headline says 98% of review-event participants rated the restaurant higher than their real satisfaction (another report says close to 99%). KCA said it would recommend that platforms mark reviews written for an event, let users edit reviews, and improve the star system. Whether the label was implemented was not verified.
findings.relevance: Star averages and shares of 5-star reviews on Korean delivery and commerce apps are contaminated by incentives: never use them as satisfaction or preference evidence (already E for population claims in source-grading.md section 3), use review text only, and add an 'incentivised review' cue ('리뷰 이벤트', '포토리뷰 이벤트', '리뷰 작성 시 증정') as a flag that caps the item at D when visible.

findings.topic: T2-7 promotion | Naver Blog and Naver Place disclosure policies
findings.finding: News reports (Nov 2024): from December 2024 Naver Blog requires posts written for economic consideration to show the disclosure in the title or first part; future or conditional compensation (commission on sales through purchase links) counts; wordings such as '업체에서 제품을 보내주셨다', '체험단' or '소정의 수수료를 지급 받을 수 있음' are reported as not acceptable, while '업체로부터 원고료를 제공받아 작성된 글' and '링크를 통해 결제가 이뤄지면 수수료를 지급받는다' are acceptable; sanctions run from warnings to deletion or hiding of posts. Marketing blogs report a Naver Place review policy change effective 2025-05-12 in which visit-verified receipt reviews (영수증 리뷰) are separate from 체험단 reviews and paid reviewers must still show the KFTC disclosure. The Naver policy pages were not readable.
findings.relevance: Since 2024-12 compliant paid Naver posts put the disclosure in the first lines, so the reader should look there; a post with a coupon or affiliate link and a disclosure only at the end is non-compliant, not necessarily organic. A visit-verified review is better evidence of firsthand use than an unverified one (still voice, cap B). Naver Place details are single-source marketing material: treat as low.

findings.topic: T2-8 promotion | Sellers must now disclose how they handle reviews (전자상거래법 제21조의4)
findings.finding: 전자상거래법 제21조의4 (정보의 투명성 확보 조치; in the version promulgated 2026-01-20 and in force from 2026-07-21): 'e-commerce businesses and mail-order sellers that publish consumers' reviews (사용후기) on their cyber-mall must disclose the review-handling information: posting period, rating and deletion criteria, and the objection procedure when a review is deleted', with details set by decree. Failure to disclose is an administrative fine of up to 10 million won (제4항 제8호).
findings.relevance: A seller's review board is curated by the seller. Since 2026-07-21 the seller must publish how; use that notice to judge whether missing complaints mean anything, and cite it with KFTC's 2016 guideline on unreasonable deletion of unfavourable reviews. Grade first-party review boards as voice with a curation caveat and prefer independent channels.

findings.topic: T2-9 promotion | The astroturf ecosystem in Korean communities and detection flags
findings.finding: Commercial pages openly sell 'community infiltration' (침투) viral marketing in 맘카페, regional cafes and other communities: review-style (후기성), question-style and promotion-style posts; one describes using sub-accounts to post follow-up questions and reactions to prolong a thread. 체험단 platforms recruit bloggers by operating history and visitor counts and give campaign guidelines with key messages. The KFTC treats agency-scripted posts and staff posts as deceptive ads (T2-2). Flags cited by Korean news and academic pieces - accounts made for one review, bursts of near-identical reviews, generic non-specific praise - are unvalidated. These pages are marketing self-descriptions: evidence that the practice is sold, not of how common it is.
findings.relevance: Grading: count near-identical text as one unit (already in the skill); in the counter-search look for asker plus answerer pairs in one thread that praise the same product; treat bursts and new-account patterns only as flags needing independent corroboration; do not accuse individuals, record 'promotion signal' with the marker and its location.

findings.topic: T2-10 promotion | 내돈내산 is a claim, not evidence; suggested marker changes
findings.finding: 내돈내산 spread as a self-declared non-ad tag after the 2020 뒷광고 controversy, and the government legal-information portal's own headline is '내돈 내산 알고 보면 뒷광고, 규제강화'. Combined with T2-1 the KFTC rule is that a review must match a real experience and any economic interest must be disclosed, whatever tag the post carries.
findings.relevance: Treat 내돈내산, '광고 아님', '협찬 아님' and '직접 구매' as claims that carry no weight in grading. Suggested edits to markers.json (verify on a corpus): add the KFTC-clear forms listed in T2-1; keep '체험단' forms as promotion signals; add incentivised-review cues from T2-6; add 'AI 가상인물' disclosure forms from the 2026 rule.

findings.topic: T3-1 quantitative | Statistics Act rules and 2025-10-01 agency renamings (org aliases)
findings.finding: 통계법 (Act 21575 of 2026-04-21, in force 2026-07-22): the head of 국가데이터처 designates (제17조) and approves (제18조) statistics; approval may be refused where the sample is too small, the method unproven, or the purpose commercial; publishers must publish each statistic together with its target and method (제27조 2항), so every approved statistic has a 통계설명자료 stating n, frame and error. 국가데이터처 (English: Ministry of Data and Statistics, MODS) is the former 통계청 (renamed 2025-10-01); other 2025-10-01 renamings visible in statute texts: 방송통신위원회 -> 방송미디어통신위원회 (방미통위, KMCC) and 특허청 -> 지식재산처. KOSIS is run by 국가데이터처 with 한국통계정보원; a Seoul Economic Daily headline of 2026-09-28 reports a further merger of two statistics bodies (details not read).
findings.relevance: source-grading.md section 5 says 'Statistics Korea's site and KOSIS: set org to Statistics Korea': update the org alias table so 통계청, Statistics Korea, 국가데이터처, MODS, kostat.go.kr and mods.go.kr are one organisation, and cite the agency name valid on the publication date. For any size claim, require the statistic's approval number and its 통계설명자료 (n, frame, sampling error) instead of a press summary.

findings.topic: T3-2 quantitative | KOSIS: what it is, what it supports, how to call it
findings.finding: KOSIS (국가통계포털, kosis.kr) is a portal that hosts approved statistics from many agencies (population, employment, surveys), not a survey. Its Open API (공유서비스) needs a member key (one key per member, all services) and offers statistics list, statistics data, bulk data, statistics description, table description, integrated search and key indicators in JSON, XML, XLS and SDMX; one data call returns at most 40,000 cells; a notice on per-minute call limits was posted 2026-07-09 (details not read); a third-party page says development keys have a daily cap of about 10,000 (unverified). CSV copies of several surveys are on data.go.kr under 공공누리 (type not verified).
findings.relevance: Use KOSIS for population denominators (age x sex x region) and for approved surveys it hosts; each table's metadata gives n and reference period. Statistical family: it bounds segment_share or device_mix for the population it covers (max B), never a product's users. The R0 'official API with the user's own key' rung fits (key from an environment variable); respect the per-minute limit.

findings.topic: T3-3 quantitative | 인터넷이용실태조사 (MSIT with NIA), 2025 wave
findings.finding: Survey on the Internet Usage (reported as 국가승인통계 제120005호): 2025 results published 2026-03-31 - 22,671 households and 50,750 household members aged 3+; 99.98% of households have internet access; 95.0% of people aged 3+ use the internet (+0.5 pt); 44.5% have used generative AI (33.3% a year earlier); average 21.6 hours per week. It covers devices, places, purposes, services (SNS, cloud, AI) and age groups, is yearly, and tables are on data.go.kr as CSV.
findings.relevance: Best national denominator for 'who is online, uses a smartphone or AI' by age (3+ frame). Supports segment_share and device_mix bounds and context_of_use at population level (statistical, max B); cannot say how many use a given product. Sampling error and fieldwork dates were not confirmed: take them from the 통계설명자료 before stating a margin.

findings.topic: T3-4 quantitative | 디지털정보격차 실태조사 (MSIT with NIA; approved statistic 120017)
findings.finding: About 15,000 respondents interviewed face to face across 17 regions in deliberately unequal strata: general public 7,000 (of whom 2,300 aged 55+), people with disabilities 2,200, low-income 2,200, farmers and fishers 2,200, North Korean defectors 700, marriage migrants 700. The index has 25 self-report items combined as access 0.2 + competency 0.4 + use 0.4 and is expressed against the general public = 100. Running since 2002, approved since 2006. 2025 results (published 2026-03-26): vulnerable groups at 77.9% of the general public (+0.4 pt, fifth consecutive year of improvement).
findings.relevance: Use for digital-competence assumptions of older, disabled, low-income and rural personas (condition_presence or condition_share limited to the surveyed group, statistical B). Strata are oversampled and unequal, so never compute population shares from the raw n, and note 'elderly' here means 55+, not 65+. Subgroup values (for example older adults' level) were not retrieved: fill docs/human-factors/korean-population-context.md row 19 from the official tables.

findings.topic: T3-5 quantitative | Web accessibility survey and smartphone over-dependence (same MSIT/NIA releases)
findings.finding: Web accessibility (surveyed sites scored against KWCAG 2.2): mean 53.7 in 2019; 66.7 in 2024 (+0.9; published 2025-03-27; education services highest 76.9, real estate lowest 60.5, firms with 50-99 employees highest 76.4); 70.4 in 2025 (+3.7; published 2026-03-26). Arithmetic check 70.4 - 3.7 = 66.7; one search summary that gave 66.7 for 2025 mixed years. Smartphone over-dependence (2025): 22.7% of smartphone users at risk (22.9% in 2024, peak 24.2% in 2021), teens 10-19 at 43.0%, children 3-9 at 26.0%.
findings.relevance: A sourced baseline for persona-qa expectations: an average Korean site scores about 70 out of 100 on KWCAG. It is an estimate for the population of sites, not of users. Over-dependence rates come from a self-report screening scale: context for time-pressure and attention personas, not prevalence of a UX condition.

findings.topic: T3-6 quantitative | 방송매체 이용행태조사 (방미통위 with KAIT), 2025 wave
findings.finding: Published 2025-12-30 as national approved statistics: 5,566 households and 8,320 people aged 13+ interviewed in person across 17 regions. Smartphone use flat, TV use up (the gap narrowed), about 8 in 10 use OTT with rising OTT viewing on TVs, pay-TV subscription falling, online audio use 20.1% (+1.7 pt). Data files on data.go.kr (dataset 3068653). The issuer was 방송통신위원회 until its 2025-10-01 renaming, so older tables carry the old name.
findings.relevance: Frame is 13+: use for media and device context of use (statistical B bound), for example TV as a screen for OTT apps, not for app-level share. Fieldwork dates and sampling error were not confirmed.

findings.topic: T3-7 quantitative | 한국소비자원 (KCA): three kinds of evidence, and one design pitfall
findings.finding: (1) 1372 consumer-centre statistics on data.go.kr (counts by item, region, age group, monthly): complaint counts from people who chose to call, i.e. a voice source, not prevalence (Aug 2026: 51,443 calls, -6.6% month on month). (2) Policy indicators 소비생활지표, 소비자시장평가지표, 소비자역량지수, with questionnaires and micro-data published (data.go.kr 15064827). (3) Topic surveys with stated n: 2022 kiosk study - 500 kiosk users aged 20s-60s, 100 per decade; 46.6% (233) had inconvenience or harm in the past year; reasons: pressure from people behind (52.8%), difficult operation (46.8%), device errors (39.1%); among 60+, difficult operation 53.6% and small text 23.2%. A separate 65+ survey (n=300; 245 kiosk users) found 51.4% complex steps, 51% could not find the next-step button, 49% felt rushed by people behind; in a small observation test all five participants aged 70+ failed to finish payment, and older adults struggled with English menu terms and 초성 search.
findings.relevance: Equal-quota cells (100 per decade) support within-band rates, not a population rate: the 46.6% is not a national prevalence (my inference from the design). Use as measured or statistical evidence for pain_point and context_of_use (B), state n and band, note 눈치 (social pressure from the queue) as a Korean context factor for personas, and treat 초성-search difficulty as a concrete UX cue for older personas. The original reports were not read (kca.go.kr blocked).

findings.topic: T3-8 quantitative | 게임이용자 실태조사 (KOCCA/MCST) 2025
findings.finding: Published 2025-12-18; about 10,000 respondents aged 10-69 (design details unverified). Game use in the past year 50.2% (down 9.7 pt); by platform (among players) mobile 89.1%, PC 58.1%, console 28.6%, arcade 10.4%, VR 6.3%; one social-media relay of the report gives 62.8% Nintendo, 49% PlayStation, 15.3% Xbox among console players (single secondary source).
findings.relevance: Fills docs/human-factors/korean-population-context.md row 26 (was NOT RETRIEVED). Statistical family: a bound for device_mix among game players (B); sampling frame and weights need checking in the report before use.

findings.topic: T3-9 quantitative | Age frames differ between the Korean sources
findings.finding: Internet-use survey: aged 3+. Media survey: 13+. Game survey: 10-69. Digital-divide survey: 'elderly' = 55+. KCA older-adult kiosk work: 65+. Over-dependence bands: 3-9 and 10-19. KCA kiosk quotas: 20s-60s.
findings.relevance: audience-pipeline: state the frame (age range, household or person, reference period, weights) with every statistical value and never add or compare shares across frames; if a persona says 'senior', record which threshold (55, 60, 65) the source used. Add 'frame' and 'reference period' fields to the statistical evidence in the bundle.

findings.topic: T4-1 KWCAG | Identity, structure and history of KWCAG 2.2
findings.finding: KWCAG 2.2 (한국형 웹 콘텐츠 접근성 지침 2.2) is the national web-accessibility standard KS X OT0003:2022 (broadcasting-communications standard series KCS.OT-10.0003/R3), owned by MSIT's 국립전파연구원 and issued by the 방송통신표준심의회; revised 2022-12-28, replacing KS X OT0003:2015. Structure: 4 principles, 14 guidelines, 33 check items (I counted all 33 headings) - 24 from the previous edition plus 9 new: 6.1.4 character-key shortcuts, 6.4.4 fixed reference locator, 6.5.1 single-pointer input, 6.5.2 pointer cancellation, 6.5.3 label in name, 6.5.4 motion actuation, 7.2.2 findable help, 7.3.3 accessible authentication, 7.3.4 redundant entry. History: first issued 2005-12-21; 2010 revision followed WCAG 2.0; 2015-03-31 revision added mobile items. The standard says it can serve as the standard for the web-accessibility duties under the (old) Intelligent Informatization Act and the Anti-Discrimination Act. Read from the a11ykr unofficial online edition (byte-identical on re-download), which says it is not official; the official copy is at rra.go.kr.
findings.relevance: The repo docs' 'KWCAG 2.2 = KS X OT0003:2022, 33 items' is confirmed. Cite the official RRA copy in reports and mark a11ykr as a convenience mirror. In the online edition the contrast item is mis-numbered '1.4.3' (it is 5.4.3): check item numbers against the PDF before quoting.

findings.topic: T4-2 KWCAG | How KWCAG relates to WCAG (numbers do not line up)
findings.finding: KWCAG version numbers do not follow WCAG's: KWCAG 2.1 (2015) tracked WCAG 2.0; KWCAG 2.2 (2022) was written on the basis of WCAG 2.1 (2018), centred on Level A success criteria and the mandatory items, with domestic conditions in mind. The five Level-A criteria added in WCAG 2.1 (2.1.4, 2.5.1-2.5.4) became KWCAG 6.1.4 and 6.5.1-6.5.4. Three further new KWCAG items match WCAG 2.2 criteria that are not in WCAG 2.1: 7.2.2 = 3.2.6 Consistent Help, 7.3.4 = 3.3.7 Redundant Entry, 7.3.3 about 3.3.8/3.3.9 Accessible Authentication; 6.4.4 (page-break locators for e-publications) has no WCAG counterpart; 8.1.1 markup-error prevention is a Parsing-type item. WCAG 2.2 (W3C Recommendation 2023-10-05) adds nine criteria - 2.4.11, 2.4.12, 2.4.13, 2.5.7, 2.5.8, 3.2.6, 3.3.7, 3.3.8, 3.3.9 - and marks 4.1.1 Parsing obsolete (2023-01-25); the W3C source has 87 criterion entries (61 from 2.0, 17 from 2.1, 9 from 2.2), 86 excluding 4.1.1.
findings.relevance: KWCAG 2.2 is not WCAG 2.2 AA and conformance to one does not imply the other: run both rule sets and report them separately (matches the contradiction table in docs/human-factors/ux-design-discipline.md). When a Korean client says 'we meet 웹접근성 2.2' it means the 33-item standard.

findings.topic: T4-3 KWCAG | Items where KWCAG text differs from WCAG in ways testers hit
findings.finding: 5.4.3 contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 for text of 18 pt or larger, bold 14 pt, or zoomable text) matches WCAG 1.4.3 AA. 6.1.3 asks controls to be at least 6.0 mm on the diagonal (desirable, not mandatory) with a 1 px non-reactive inner margin: a physical-size rule in mm unlike WCAG 2.5.8's 24 CSS px. 6.3.1 forbids content that flashes 3-50 times per second (WCAG 2.3.1 uses the three-flashes or threshold test). 5.4.2 forbids autoplaying sound (up to 3 s tolerated, else a control); 5.4.4 requires adjacent content to be distinguishable (borders, spacing), which has no WCAG twin. From the 33 item titles there are no counterparts to WCAG's AA additions: reflow, text spacing, non-text contrast, orientation, status messages, target size (minimum), focus not obscured, dragging alternatives; KWCAG does import some AA content (contrast, visible focus in 6.1.2, accessible authentication).
findings.relevance: human-factors-checks.md PC-01 and ux-design-discipline.md already cite several of these. Keep the two-standard report format ('KWCAG 2.2 item X' and 'WCAG 2.2 SC Y') and never claim a page 'complies with Korean law' from tool output: legal conformity is judged against the statutes and MSIT notices (T4-4).

findings.topic: T4-4 KWCAG | Legal hooks: 장애인차별금지법, 디지털포용법
findings.finding: 장애인차별금지법 제21조(1): parties that produce or distribute electronic information must let disabled people access it equally; 시행령 제14조(2)1 names as a required means 'a website whose accessibility is guaranteed so that anyone, regardless of physical or technical conditions, can use the service' (phased scope in 별표 3, not read). Since 2021-07-27 제21조(2) covers mobile apps: 시행령 제14조(6) (from 2023-03-30, amended 2025-12-31) requires compliance with the MSIT verification criteria set under 디지털포용법 시행령 제24조(2), an indication before purchase or install of whether they are met, information by disability type, text, sign or voice help, and voice-command support. 디지털포용법 (Act 20672, promulgated 2025-01-21, in force 2026-01-22; it deleted 지능정보화 기본법 제46-49조): 제19조 obliges state bodies to ensure accessibility of websites, apps, unmanned kiosks and e-publications and asks private operators to make efforts; 제21조 sets accessibility quality certification (valid one year under decree 제21조) and transitional rules keep earlier certifying bodies. The statutes do not name KWCAG; the standard reaches practice through MSIT notices, certification and the annual web-accessibility survey.
findings.relevance: persona-qa and ergonomics reports can cite the statutory duty and the KWCAG standard separately; mobile apps are judged by MSIT criteria rather than KWCAG (KS X 3253 is mentioned in repo docs but unverified here). The phased-scope tables (별표 3, 3의2) and the MSIT notices were not available in the mirror.

findings.topic: T5-1 law | 정보통신망법 제48조 and penalties (verbatim text, versions)
findings.finding: Text (identical in the 2026-01-06, 2026-03-10 and 2026-03-31 versions; the 2026-03-10 version is in force on 2026-09-29, the 2026-03-31 version takes effect 2026-10-01): 제48조 ① '누구든지 정당한 접근권한 없이 또는 허용된 접근권한을 넘어 정보통신망에 침입하여서는 아니 된다.' ③ '누구든지 정보통신망의 안정적 운영을 방해할 목적으로 대량의 신호 또는 데이터를 보내거나 부정한 명령을 처리하도록 하는 등의 방법으로 정보통신망에 장애가 발생하게 하여서는 아니 된다.' ④ (added 2024-01-23) '누구든지 정당한 사유 없이 정보통신망의 정상적인 보호·인증 절차를 우회하여 정보통신망에 접근할 수 있도록 하는 프로그램이나 기술적 장치 등을 정보통신망 또는 이와 관련된 정보시스템에 설치하거나 이를 전달·유포하여서는 아니 된다.' Penalty 제71조(1) items 11-13: up to 5 years or 50 million won; an attempt at ① is punishable (제71조(2)). Older judgments cite the same offence as 제71조(1)9 because of renumbering.
findings.relevance: public-page-access.md section 17 mentions Art. 48 in one line. Expand: ① is the offence tested in 2021도1533 and 2023도1086; ③ is why one-request-per-host pacing and budgets matter; ④ makes providing or distributing bypass tooling a separate offence. Together with the (카)목(4) rule (T5-7) this raises the legal risk of the opt-in R4 engine rung (browser-equivalent TLS fingerprint to pass bot filters), which also conflicts with the owner's no-evasion boundary: recommend dropping R4 or hard-disabling it, at least for Korean hosts. Not legal advice; ④ has no reported case yet.

findings.topic: T5-2 law | Supreme Court 2022-05-12, 2021도1533 (Yanolja/Goodchoice crawling), read in full
findings.finding: The prosecutor's appeal was dismissed (상고기각), so the acquittals stood on all three charges. Facts: defendants found the URL and commands of Yanolja's app API server (not actively published, but easy to find with ordinary packet-capture tools) and used a self-built crawler to pull accommodation data; ordinary users reached the API with or without membership and there was no separate protective measure. Holdings: (1) 제48조(1) intrusion - the service provider sets who may access, and whether it restricts access is judged 'by protective measures, terms of use and other objectively manifested circumstances, carefully'; a ToS clause banning commercial reuse of acquired information limits use, not access; a ToS ban on auto-access programs that overload servers could not be shown to bind non-members nor to restrict access itself -> no intrusion. (2) DB right (저작권법 제93조): 'substantial part' is judged quantitatively (against the whole DB) and qualitatively (the producer's investment in making or updating that part); repeated or systematic taking of insubstantial parts counts only if it amounts in effect to a substantial part; the lower court found the data already widely known or public, no proof of costly collection or update, and no conflict with the DB's normal use, and the Supreme Court upheld. (3) 형법 제314조(2) computer-disruption obstruction needs actual malfunction, not proven. The judgment does not mention robots.txt (checked by search of the full text). It is a criminal ruling (burden on the prosecution) on 2016 facts under the pre-2018-12-24 statute, not a licence to scrape.
findings.relevance: The test is objective access restriction plus wholesale copying. The skill's stops (login, paywall, CAPTCHA, robots disallow, rate limit) are the kind of 'objectively manifested' restrictions, so honouring them keeps the tool outside 제48조(1). Cite this case in public-page-access.md section 17; never paraphrase it as 'crawling is legal'.

findings.topic: T5-3 law | Follow-on Supreme Court rulings: 2023도1086 and 2023도17354 (read in full)
findings.finding: 2023-10-26, 2023도1086: reaffirmed the 2021도1533 test and reversed a conviction where a person changed the last two digits of a URL to view colleagues' evaluation pages that needed no login or authentication and had no protection limiting access to the individual; the operator itself had been convicted under the PIPA for missing safeguards. The Court also read 제49조 narrowly: 'infringement' and 'leaking' of another's secret require acquiring it by intrusion or other improper means. 2024-04-16, 2023도17354: a 저작권법 DB-right conviction was upheld where the defendant copied a whole construction-cost database (table-name similarity 90%, schema 98.2%, data 90.4%); the producer had invested in staff, monthly updates and paid sources, and the Court restated the quantitative and qualitative test and that repeated or systematic taking of insubstantial parts counts only if it amounts to a substantial part.
findings.relevance: The line drawn is objective access restriction plus wholesale copying, not robots.txt (not mentioned in any of the three judgments). 2023도1086 is not an invitation to enumerate or guess URLs: the skill's rule against undocumented endpoints stays, and civil and PIPA exposure remain. 2023도17354 shows that copying a whole database is punishable, which is why sampling, per-host budgets and no republication matter.

findings.topic: T5-4 law | Acquittal did not end civil exposure (Yanolja civil case; Jobkorea v. Saramin)
findings.finding: Yanolja v. Goodchoice civil case for the same 2016 crawling: Seoul High Court 2022-08-25, 2021나2034740 (on law.go.kr as 판례 226943, '데이터베이스제작자의권리침해금지등') - per news and law-firm summaries an injunction plus 1,000,000,000 won (1 billion won; one English summary wrote '10 billion' by mistake) with interest, the first instance having found unfair-competition performance misappropriation rather than a DB-right infringement. Jobkorea v. Saramin: Seoul High Court 2017-04-06, 2016나2019365, 저작권법 제93조(1),(2) infringement where 396 job postings were copied and republished with only the brand name removed (even typos identical), 198 million won; the Supreme Court dismissed the appeal under the special act on appeals. Decisions themselves were not read.
findings.relevance: The risk pattern is wholesale copying for a competing service, not analysing a sample; still, keep public-page-access.md section 17's warning that terms of service and unfair-competition law can apply even where no crime is found.

findings.topic: T5-5 law | Database-producer rights (저작권법 제93-95조) and the research exception
findings.finding: 저작권법 (version in force: Act 21336 of 2026-02-10, effective 2026-08-11; the 2026-04-28 Act changes only collective-management provisions): 제2조(19) 데이터베이스 = 소재를 체계적으로 배열 또는 구성한 편집물로서 개별적으로 그 소재에 접근하거나 그 소재를 검색할 수 있도록 한 것; (20) 데이터베이스제작자 = 제작 또는 갱신·검증·보충에 인적 또는 물적으로 상당한 투자를 한 자. 제93조(1) right to reproduce, distribute, broadcast or transmit all or a substantial part; (2) individual materials are not a substantial part, but repeated or systematic reproduction of individual materials or insubstantial parts counts as a substantial part when it conflicts with the DB's 'general use' (일반적인 이용, wording since 2023-08-08; older judgments say 통상적인) or unreasonably harms the producer; (4) the protection does not reach the materials themselves. 제94조(1) quotation (제28조), private use (제30조) and fair use (제35조의5) apply mutatis mutandis; 제94조(2)1 anyone may reproduce even all or a substantial part for 교육·학술·연구 unless for profit and unless it conflicts with the DB's general use. 제95조: term 5 years from the year after completion (renewed for substantially updated parts). Criminal: 제136조(3)3 up to 3 years or 30 million won; prosecution needs a complaint (제140조) unless for profit or habitual.
findings.relevance: Design consequence for a research reader: sample, do not mirror; keep per-host budgets; never republish or build a competing index. The research exception is closed to for-profit use and to copying that conflicts with the DB's general use; whether a company's UX research counts as 'for profit' is unsettled (unverified). Add to public-page-access.md section 17 in place of the one-line mention of Article 93.

findings.topic: T5-6 law | Quoting public posts: 저작권법 제28조, 제30조, 제35조의5, 제37조
findings.finding: 제28조: '공표된 저작물은 보도·비평·교육·연구 등을 위하여는 정당한 범위 안에서 공정한 관행에 합치되게 이를 인용할 수 있다.' Supreme Court 2013-02-15, 2011도5835: the purpose list is not exhaustive, but the 'legitimate range' requires the quoted work to be accessory (부종적: 보족, 부연, 예증, 참고자료) to the quoting work, judged by purpose, nature of the work, amount and content quoted, manner of inclusion, readers' general perception and whether it substitutes for demand for the original; copying inside a company for business use is not 'private use' (제30조 covers only non-profit personal or household use); the general fair-use clause (now 제35조의5, four factors) exists only since the 2011-12-02 amendment. 제37조(1)-(2): whoever uses a work under these limits must state the source in a reasonable way and, where the work shows the author's real name or pseudonym, must state it. The current text has no text-and-data-mining or AI provision (searched: zero matches); the MCST and Korea Copyright Commission guidance of 2026-02-26 on fair use for generative-AI training is non-binding and applies 제35조의5.
findings.relevance: Default to paraphrase in shared outputs; keep verbatim excerpts (at most 300 characters, 5 per source) inside the run and bundle and attribute by channel, date and source ID as today; record that 제37조(2)'s name-or-pseudonym rule is not met by handle-stripping (my analysis; unverified whether a URL-based source credit satisfies it for a pseudonymous post): a decision for counsel. A personal, non-profit copy for one's own analysis can rest on 제30조; a team using it at work cannot (2011도5835). Whether short posts or one-line reviews reach the originality threshold was not researched.

findings.topic: T5-7 law | 부정경쟁방지법 (카)목: the letters changed on 2022-04-20
findings.finding: Before 2022-04-20 the general performance-misappropriation clause ('그 밖에 타인의 상당한 투자나 노력으로 만들어진 성과 등을 공정한 상거래 관행이나 경쟁질서에 반하는 방법으로 자신의 영업을 위하여 무단으로 사용함으로써 타인의 경제적 이익을 침해하는 행위') was item (카) (version of 2020-12-22). Since the Act of 2021-12-07 (effective 2022-04-20) that clause is (파), and (카) is data misappropriation: 데이터 (Data Industry Act 제2조1호 data that is provided as a business to specific persons or specific multiple persons and accumulated and managed in bulk by electronic means; trade secrets excluded) used unfairly by (1) a person without access rights obtaining it by theft, deceit, unauthorised access (부정접속) or other improper means, or using or disclosing what was so obtained; (2) an authorised person using, disclosing or providing it to gain an improper benefit or harm the holder; (3) knowingly acquiring or using data from (1) or (2); (4) providing, making or transmitting technology, services or devices whose main purpose is to neutralise the technical protection applied to the data (exception: making devices for R&D of protection measures). The text is unchanged in the 2025-10-01 version and in the 2026-09-15 amendment (effective 2027-03-16), which only touches trade-secret items. Commentary (Kim & Chang, Shin & Kim, KCI articles) says data offered to unspecified members of the public is outside (카); how far 'specific multiple persons' reaches is uncertain; a 2023 article found no court decision applying (카) yet, and I found none for 2024-2026 (unverified).
findings.relevance: Cite by statute version: crawling cases from before 2022 (Yanolja, Jobkorea) used the older general clause, not today's (카). (카) matters to the skill through 'access without authority or by improper means' and the ban on tools that neutralise technical protection (4); the general clause (파) is the civil route used in crawling cases. Do not treat 'publicly reachable' as automatically outside either clause.

findings.topic: T5-8 law | 개인정보 보호법: what applies to a research tool that stores public posts
findings.finding: Text of the version in force on 2026-09-29 (Act of 2026-03-10; Arts. 2, 3, 15, 20, 23, 28-2, 37, 59 identical in the 2026-09-08 amendment). 제2조(1): personal information includes information that alone does not identify but can be easily combined with other information (judged by time, cost, technology); 가명정보 needs additional information kept apart to re-identify; 제2조(5) 개인정보처리자 = anyone who operates a personal-information file 'for business purposes' (업무를 목적으로); 제2조(8) 과학적 연구 includes 기술의 개발과 실증, 기초연구, 응용연구 and 민간 투자 연구 applying scientific methods. 제3조(1),(6),(7): minimum data, least intrusive method, anonymise or pseudonymise where the purpose can still be met. 제15조(1)6: legitimate interest that clearly overrides the data subject's rights. 제20조(1): on request, notify the source, the purpose and the right to suspend; proactive notice only for controllers with sensitive or ID-number data on 50,000+ people or any data on 1 million+ people (시행령 제15조의2). 제22조의2: under-14 needs a guardian. 제23조: sensitive information (beliefs, union or party, political views, health, sex life ...) barred without separate consent or law. 제28조의2: pseudonymised information may be processed without consent for statistics, scientific research or archiving (not a licence to collect). 제37조: suspension on request, then destruction. 제58조(1): no research exemption (only national-security analysis, press, religion, parties). 제59조(1)/제72조(2): obtaining personal information by 'false or other improper means' - up to 3 years or 30 million won; 제59조(3)/제71조(10): improper use - up to 5 years or 50 million won. The 2026-09-08 Act (No. 21910, in force 2027-03-09) adds 제2조(9) and 제28조의12-14, special rules letting the PIPC approve purpose-changing use of lawfully collected personal information for AI development: not a licence to scrape and not relevant to analysis unless outputs train models.
findings.relevance: A stored post with URL and content is likely personal information whenever the poster can be identified; the salted author key plus the URL together are pseudonymous at best, because the URL is the 'additional information' that re-identifies (so the run-folder deletion at close or 72 h is a real safeguard). Keep minimisation (no handles, profile links, sensitive or minor content, no post history of one person), build a deletion and 제20조 response path, and note that PIPA gives a research tool no exemption. Whether the tool operator is a 개인정보처리자 depends on 'business purpose' (a company or institute: yes; pure hobby use: probably not; unverified).

findings.topic: T5-9 law | Case law on already-public personal information
findings.finding: Supreme Court 2016-08-17, 2014다235080 (로앤비): information formed in public life or already disclosed is still protected; but the PIPA does not separate disclosed from undisclosed data for 제15조/제17조, and processing within the range objectively regarded as consented to at disclosure needs no separate consent; that range is judged by the nature of the information, the form and audience of disclosure, the person's disclosure purpose, the form of processing, whether the audience changes, and the relation to the original purpose; protection then works as 'post-control' through 제20조 (source, purpose, suspension right). Where profit-making use of disclosed data is challenged, the court balances (public figure, publicness, original audience, purpose, procedure, form, interests); profit alone does not make it unlawful; a paid directory built from law professors' public profile data was lawful. Supreme Court 2011-09-02, 2008다42430 (en banc): a lawyers' 'networking index' built from personal data was unlawful (majority), while win-rate and expertise indices built from public court data were lawful.
findings.relevance: Risk sits where a public post is reused for a different purpose or audience (for example a named quote in a client report) and where new derived facts about a person are created. Aggregated, unnamed use for the same topic the poster wrote about fits the 'objectively consented range' best. Keep a takedown path (제20조, 제37조) and prefer paraphrase.

findings.topic: T5-10 law | PIPC guides on public personal information and scraping (read as text)
findings.finding: Read via third-party GitHub text extractions of the official PDFs (발간등록번호 11-1790365-000032-01, July 2024; 11-1790365-100030-01, Aug 2025). 2024 public-information guide: '공개된 개인정보' = personal information anyone can lawfully access, not only what the person posted (also legally published data, publications, broadcasts); collecting, storing and pre-processing are 'processing'; the basis to examine is 제15조(1)6 (legitimate purpose, necessity and proportionality, clearly overriding the data subject's rights) with technical and managerial safeguards; the Supreme Court's six consent-scope factors are borrowed as supplementary balancing factors, and terms of use or privacy policies that show wide sharing support a broad reading (Seoul High Court 2015노1998, the Twitter case). For scraping it says comply with the site's terms of use and the robots exclusion standard, skip domains that trade illegal data, avoid sites that aggregate personal data, respect IP rights, and publish the collection standards (for example robots compliance) if source-by-source disclosure is impractical; sensitive and children's data need stronger safeguards and should be avoided in bulk collection. It expressly does not cover other-law duties such as unauthorised access (정보통신망법 제48조), 부정경쟁방지법 제2조 and fair use (저작권법 제35조의5). The 2025-08 generative-AI guide adds that content whose owner clearly refused scraping should be excluded: terms of use excluding AI training, robots.txt, or technical blocks such as CAPTCHA (citing France's CNIL, June 2025, that scraping despite such refusal undermines reasonable expectations and the legitimate-interest balance); 'noai' or 'noimageai' meta tags are listed as publisher measures. Both address AI developers and are guidance, not statute; a consolidated PIPC guide dated 2025-07-14 also exists (not read).
findings.relevance: The strongest Korean regulator support for the skill's stop rules: PIPC names terms-of-use exclusions, robots.txt and CAPTCHA as the signals of clear refusal. Cite it in public-page-access.md section 5 and section 17 (opted_out, human_check, noai) and use it to justify recording collection standards in the access table. The guides do not license reading login-gated or opted-out pages, and they say compliance with them does not settle §48, unfair-competition or copyright duties.
sources: https://github.com/Jch-Lee/Fin_AI_Challenge/blob/main/data/processed/인공지능(AI) 개발·서비스를 위한 공개된 개인정보 처리 안내서(디자인).txt

findings.topic: T5-11 law | Sending excerpts to a cloud LLM can be a cross-border transfer question
findings.finding: PIPA 제28조의8(1): providing (including making viewable), entrusting processing or storing personal information abroad is forbidden unless a listed basis applies (separate consent; contract performance with privacy-policy or direct notice; PIPC-recognised certification or adequacy; ...). PIPC's 2025-08 guide on service-type LLMs (API use): companies should review whether the provider stores or re-uses data (including training), consider enterprise API licences that exclude storage and training, fix ownership, re-use limits, safeguards and deletion in enterprise terms and a data-processing addendum, and, if the LLM server is abroad, check whether it is a 국외 이전. It cites two non-public PIPC decisions: 2024-010-184 (a call-recording summary service moved call content abroad through a service-type LLM without complete privacy-policy notice, so no lawful basis under 제28조의8(1)3) and 2024-017-237 (a hospital using a personal-tier licence risked provider training use). The 2024 guide also says collecting Koreans' public data from abroad is not itself a 'transfer' (Q1).
findings.relevance: The skill hands page excerpts to LLM agents (persona agents, judges, verifiers). If an excerpt still contains personal information (nickname plus identifying content), sending it to a foreign-hosted model is a cross-border question for the person running the skill. Design: scrub before any model call (privacy.py masks handles, phones, RRN-like numbers, partial IPs), prefer paraphrase, use API or enterprise terms that exclude training, and record provider and region in the access table. These sources do not settle whether scrubbed text still counts as personal information.

findings.topic: T5-12 law | Cyber-defamation and takedown notices (임시조치)
findings.finding: 정보통신망법 제70조: intent to defame plus a public statement over an information network - true facts up to 3 years or 30 million won; false facts up to 7 years (or 10 years' suspension of qualifications) or 70 million won (amended 2026-01-06); no prosecution against the victim's express wishes (제70조(3)). 제44조의2: a person whose privacy or reputation is harmed by publicly posted information may ask the provider to delete it or post a rebuttal; the provider acts promptly and may block access temporarily (임시조치) for up to 30 days and must show the action on the board; 제44조의3 lets providers do so on their own.
findings.relevance: Explains why posts vanish or show notices and why markers.json lists 임시조치 under legal_block; keep the rule against cache and archive copies. When a report repeats a claim about a named person or business from a post, paraphrase neutrally and attribute to 'a poster' so the report does not re-publish an unproven accusation.

findings.topic: T5-13 law | Institutional ethics review (IRB) under 생명윤리법
findings.finding: 생명윤리 및 안전에 관한 법률 제2조(1): 인간대상연구 includes research using information that can identify individuals (as set by MOHW rule); 제15조(1): prior review by an institutional review board (기관위원회); 제15조(2): minimal-risk research may be exempted under MOHW rule; 시행규칙 제13조(1) (rule effective 2025-12-03) lists exemption candidates as research using information open to the general public or not collecting or recording personal identifiers, and falling into listed types, including research using existing data or documents about subjects. The IRB decides whether to exempt.
findings.relevance: Applies only where the researcher works in an institution that must have an IRB (university, hospital, research institute); a company or hobby user is probably outside (unverified). Add one line to the research brief: 'Institutional ethics review: not required / exempt (IRB decision) / approved', and use the tool's design (public pages only, no identifiers) as the argument for exemption.

findings.topic: T5-14 law | Plain-language implications for a small, non-commercial UX research tool (my synthesis; not legal advice)
findings.finding: (1) Read only what an anonymous ordinary visitor can read; treat login, paywall, CAPTCHA, 403 or bot filter, robots.txt and terms-of-use exclusions as stops - these are the 'objectively manifested' restrictions of 2021도1533 and 2023도1086 and the 'clear refusal' signals of the PIPC guides; never install or share bypass tooling (정보통신망법 제48조(4); 부정경쟁방지법 (카)(4)). (2) Be gentle: one request at a time, human pace, budgets (제48조(3) needs intent to disrupt and 형법 제314조(2) needs actual malfunction; a polite reader is far from both). (3) Sample, do not harvest or republish and never build a competing index (저작권법 제93조; Jobkorea; Yanolja civil case). (4) Posts are copyright works and often personal information: minimise, pseudonymise, paraphrase by default, keep short verbatim excerpts internal, delete run data (72 h), honour deletion requests (PIPA 제20조, 제37조), skip sensitive and minor content and never collect one person's post history. (5) Scrub personal information before any call to a foreign-hosted LLM (제28조의8). (6) Public availability is neither consent nor a licence: check terms and robots.txt per host and add hosts to deny_hosts on request. (7) Inside a Korean university or hospital ask the IRB (생명윤리법 제15조).
findings.relevance: Suggested replacement for the one-paragraph responsibility note in public-page-access.md section 17, keeping the 'not legal advice' line, with each rule tied to the statute or judgment above. Also align the owner's no-evasion boundary with SKILL.md: the current R4 exception (browser-equivalent TLS fingerprint) is the one rung that could be argued to bypass a bot filter.
